articles.standfirst: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Sevilla y al Valencia en el Estadio Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán, correspondiente a la quinta jornada de LaLiga 26/27
articles.summary: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Sevilla y al Valencia en el Estadio Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán, correspondiente a la quinta jornada de LaLiga 26/27
articles.body: El Sevilla recibe al Valencia este viernes con la intención de dar continuidad a un arranque de temporada irregular pero por encima de su rival. Los de Luis García Plaza suman dos victorias y una derrota en sus tres primeros compromisos, con seis goles a favor y cinco en contra, y llegan de empatar 1-1 ante el Espanyol. El Valencia, por su parte, atraviesa un inicio de curso muy complicado. Es colista con un solo punto tras cuatro jornadas y acaba de encajar un severo 0-5 en casa frente al Barcelona, resultado que deja a su defensa, ya mermada por las bajas de Mouctar Diakhaby, con serias dudas. Favorito para el partido entre Sevilla y Valencia Con estos antecedentes, las casas de apuestas dan como favorito al Sevilla, aunque sin una diferencia demasiado amplia teniendo en cuenta la irregularidad reciente de ambos. Codere paga la victoria del Sevilla a cuota 2.20, por 3.15 del empate y 3.30 de la victoria del cuadro che. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una de las alternativas más discutidas del encuentro. El Sevilla llega a esta quinta jornada con una defensa que todavía no ha cerrado su portería en ningún partido esta temporada, algo que invita a pensar que el Valencia podría encontrar alguna vía de gol. Sin embargo, el conjunto che solo ha anotado un tanto en sus cuatro primeros duelos, una sequía que pesa en contra de este pronóstico. Con estos datos, la balanza en las apuestas deportivas se inclina ligeramente hacia el "no": Codere paga a 1.75 que al menos uno de los dos equipos se quede sin marcar, por 1.95 si ambos consiguen ver puerta. Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta hacia un partido con cierto potencial ofensivo, sobre todo por el lado local. El Sevilla ha marcado en sus tres partidos disputados hasta ahora y superó la barrera de los 2,5 tantos en su duelo de la primera jornada. El Valencia, en cambio, apenas ha inquietado a las defensas rivales, aunque su fragilidad atrás puede compensar su sequía de gol y dejar el marcador abierto. Codere sitúa la cuota del +2.5 goles totales a 2.2, por 1.6 del caso contrario. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners se presenta como otra alternativa interesante para los apostantes. La pasada temporada en LaLiga, el Sevilla promedió 4.79 saques de esquina a favor por partido, además de conceder una media cercana a los 4.7, lo que sitúa su promedio total de córners por encuentro en torno a los 9.5. El Valencia, por su parte, se movió en cifras ligeramente superiores en el curso anterior, con 5.03 córners a favor y 5.08 en contra, es decir, un promedio total próximo a los 10.1 por partido. Con ambos equipos moviéndose en cifras parecidas y un Sevilla que suele llevar la iniciativa como local, Codere paga a 1.85 el +9.5 córners totales, por 1.90 el caso contrario.

articles.title: Golpe de mercado a última hora: Millonarios cierra el fichaje de Juan Guillermo Cuadrado
articles.standfirst: Juan Guillermo Cuadrado a Millonarios: fichaje, contrato y detalles de su llegada
articles.summary: Juan Guillermo Cuadrado a Millonarios: fichaje, contrato y detalles de su llegada
articles.body: El Fútbol Profesional Colombiano vive horas frenéticas y sacudidas en el mercado de pases. Juan Guillermo Cuadrado está listo para convertirse en nuevo jugador de Millonarios, en lo que significa uno de los movimientos más relevantes e impactantes del fútbol nacional en los últimos tiempos. El experimentado extremo antioqueño de 38 años, referente histórico de la Selección Colombia, llegará al conjunto 'Embajador' en condición de agente libre. La noticia fue revelada en El Pulso del Fútbol de Caracol Radio por su director, el periodista César Augusto Londoño, quien dio los detalles clave sobre las negociaciones avanzadas entre los directivos del cuadro azul y la agencia del jugador. "Puedo confirmar que el negocio entre Millonarios y Cuadrado está completamente cerrado y Juan Guillermo Cuadrado será jugador de Millonarios. Sin embargo, no está firmado, y en el camino pasan muchas cosas, por lo que es mejor informarlo con claridad", afirmó Londoño. Las conversaciones se aceleraron al máximo en Bogotá ante la inminente fecha límite del mercado. La ventana de pases para jugadores libres en la Liga BetPlay cierra este viernes 11 de septiembre, motivo por el cual la directiva albiazul trabajó a contra reloj para ultimar los detalles contractuales. El empresario del jugador, Andrey Martínez, fue fundamental al facilitar el acercamiento y priorizar la oferta del equipo capitalino por encima de propuestas del exterior. Tras finalizar su vínculo contractual con el Pisa de la Serie A de Italia a mediados de este año, Cuadrado quedó habilitado para negociar sin restricciones de traspaso entre clubes. A pesar de que días atrás la opción de su regreso al país parecía distante —tras no concretarse su llegada al Independiente Medellín—, la directiva de Millonarios presentó una propuesta atractiva para convencer al futbolista y su entorno de asumir el reto de jugar en la capital. El fichaje representa el regreso del antioqueño a la liga de su país natal casi dos décadas después de su partida. Cuadrado debutó como profesional en el Independiente Medellín (2008–2009), deslumbrando con su velocidad y gambeta antes de dar el salto al Calcio italiano con el Udinese.

articles.title: Dave Portnoy Picks His All-Time Michigan Football Team On 'Joel Klatt Live Show'
articles.summary: FOX Sports' Joel Klatt tasked Dave Portnoy with selecting his all-time Michigan football team during a special live edition of "The Joel Klatt Show."
articles.body: If you invite a die-hard Michigan fan to a live show and give him the chance to build his all-time Wolverines football team, you better be ready for some debate. Dave Portnoy, one of Michigan's most passionate — and outspoken — fans, was given that opportunity Thursday during a special live edition of "The Joel Klatt Show" in Ann Arbor ahead of Saturday's showdown between Michigan and Oklahoma (noon ET, FOX). Klatt asked Portnoy to select an all-time Michigan team consisting of a quarterback, running back, two wide receivers and one defensive player. Portnoy selected a recent national champion at quarterback, a legendary running back, two of the program's most dynamic receivers and perhaps the greatest player in school history on defense. Here's who made Portnoy's all-time Michigan team: QB: J.J. McCarthy, 2021-2023 Career stats: 482-of-713 passing (67.6%) for 6,226 passing yards, 49 passing TDs, and 11 INTs; 161 carries for 632 rushing yards and 10 rushing TDs. Portnoy’s thoughts: "To me, it’s a no-brainer. It’s not even close. If you’re saying you need a QB for the NFL, it’s [Tom] Brady, clearly. But [McCarthy's] record was 27-1 as a starter. You gotta remember, before he came here, we couldn’t beat Ohio State. He turned the whole program around. Michigan was down, and when McCarthy came in, everything turned. "I wanted Jim Harbaugh gone. … Every year we were getting drummed [by Ohio State]. There were some down years. But, McCarthy’s record, him winning the national championship. … I don’t know how anybody could say anybody but him." RB: Tim Biakabutuka, 1993-1995 Career stats: 434 carries, 2,624 rushing yards, 24 rushing touchdowns, 12 receptions, 121 receiving yards. Portnoy’s Thoughts: "I’m going with Biakabutuka. He had 313 yards against Ohio State, which was the No. 2 team in the country at the time and undefeated. He made them look bad. I loved Biakabutuka. I had a crush on Biakabutuka." WRs: Desmond Howard ( 1988-91), Anthony Carter (1979-82) Career stats: Howard: 134 receptions for 2,146 receiving yards (16.0 YPR) and 32 receiving TDs; 23 rushes for 249 rushing yards and 2 rushing TDs; 45 kickoff returns for 1,211 yards and 2 TDs; 26 punt returns for 337 yards and 1 TDCarter: 161 receptions for 3,076 receiving yards (19.1 YPR) and 37 receiving TDs; 36 rushes for 213 rushing yards and 1 rushing TD; 79 punt returns for 907 yards and 2 TDs; 63 kickoff returns for 1,606 yards (40 total touchdowns). Portnoy's thoughts: "I want Desmond [Howard] and Anthony Carter. I’m down with that." Defense: Charles Woodson, 1995-1997 Career stats: 21 receptions, 370 receiving yards, 3 receiving TDs, 167 rushing yards, 2 rushing TDs, 16 interceptions. Portnoy’s thoughts: "You could argue Aidan Hutchinson. There’s that clip of him just taking the Ohio State lineman and just throwing him into the fourth row. But, yeah, it’s gotta be Woodson."

articles.title: Polygraph Tests & Michigan All-Time Team: Scenes From The Joel Klatt Show In Ann Arbor
articles.summary: From Polygraph tests to an all-time Michigan team, here are the best moments from "The Joel Klatt Show" live from Ann Arbor.
articles.body: There aren't many better ways to get ready for a major college football tilt than a live show before the game. Ahead of Michigan hosting No. 11 Oklahoma this Saturday, FOX Sports college football analyst Joel Klatt hosted a live showing of "The Joel Klatt Show" in Ann Arbor. The third-ever live "Joel Klatt Show" sold out The Circ Bar and featured guest stars like a national title-winning head coach and Klatt's "Big Noon Kickoff" colleagues. Klatt hosted guests including former Oklahoma coach Bob Stoops, FOX Sports' Jenny Taft and "Big Noon Kickoff's" Dave Portnoy. Klatt and co. discussed everything from the 24-team playoff to expectations for Michigan against Oklahoma and even put them in the spotlight with a lie-detector test. Here are the best moments from "The Joel Klatt Show" live in Ann Arbor: Dave Portnoy Reveals His All-Time Michigan Team It's no secret that Portnoy is a passionate Michigan football fan, portraying his fandom constantly on-air and on social media. On Klatt's live show, Portnoy revealed his all-time Michigan team with his top-five Wolverine players of all time. To name a few, Portnoy included players from the Wolverines' recent national title win in 2023, like quarterback J.J. McCarthy, and their 1997 national title team with Heisman winner Charles Woodson. Portnoy's all-time Michigan team: Quarterback: J.J. McCarthy Wide receivers: Desmond Howard, Anthony Carter Running back: Tim Biakabutuka Defense: Charles Woodson Portnoy Wanted WHO Gone? Following his all-time Michigan team, Portnoy shared his thoughts on former Michigan coach Jim Harbaugh, who led the Wolverines to a national title in 2024. Harbaugh finished his coaching tenure at Michigan with an 86-25 overall record, a 60-17 record in conference play and three consecutive Big Ten Championships from 2021-23. Harbaugh's final year saw a Big Ten title, an undefeated 15-0 record and a national title win. Despite the success, Portnoy's thoughts on Harbaugh did not change. "Once McCarthy came in, everything changed. Hand up, I wanted Harbaugh gone," Portnoy said. "It was every year we were getting drummed. I bet there are a lot of silent Michigan fans out there that are like, ‘Yeah, maybe we thought it was time for a change.’ There were some down years." Bob Stoops Joins, Weighs In On 24-Team Playoff Former Oklahoma coach Bob Stoops joined Klatt and Portnoy on stage and weighed in on current topics surrounding the college football landscape. Stoops was head coach of the Sooners from 1999-2016 and compiled a 191-48 overall record, two Big 12 titles and a BCS National Championship in 2000. In particular, Stoops shared his thoughts on the possible College Football Playoff expansion to 24 teams. "I've been a proponent of less playoff games, but these games are going to go away. So then that would be the reason to keep the 24 teams in the playoff," Stoops said. "Because now you can come up to Michigan, things don't go the right way, you can still recover from it." Portnoy, Klatt Take Polygraph Test If you've seen Zlatan's infamous Polygraph test during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, get ready for Klatt and Portnoy to have their turn. Klatt went first, and was asked about everything from his Big Noon Kickoff colleagues and the success at his alma mater, Colorado. However, one answer regarding Saturday's matchup stood out. When Portnoy asked Klatt about his stance on Michigan beating the No. 11 Sooners, his answer was simple and true. "Do you think Michigan can actually win [on] Saturday?" Portnoy asked. "Yes," Klatt said confidently. When it was time for Portnoy to take the test, the focus was not so much on his Wolverines' upcoming matchup. Portnoy was instantly asked by Taft how his last weekend went when Rutgers was upset by UMass in Week 1. articles.title: 49ers Dominate Down Under: 3 Takeaways From The Niners' Win Over The Rams
articles.summary: The NFL's first-ever game in Australia took place on Friday morning in Melbourne.
articles.body: Let’s slow the "super team" chatter around the Los Angeles Rams. Just for now. Australia was not good to the Rams, who looked tired and sloppy in their season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers. The Niners took total control of the game, largely by controlling the line of scrimmage. By the fourth quarter, the Rams never really knocked on contention — slipping deeper and deeper into defeat. It’s important to remember that Week 1 lies. In other words, there’s a long, long season ahead. And this game — which took place roughly 8,000 miles from Los Angeles — won’t tell us everything we need to know about either team. But there’s no denying it: the 49ers looked dominant. And the Rams looked … dominated. Here are my takeaways: 1.Despite Injuries, Brock Purdy Has More Playmakers Than He Needs It was brutal to watch rookie receiver De’Zhaun Stribling get carted off with an injury in the first half. That’s another injury to another young receiver — after wide receiver Ricky Pearsall headed to IR before the season started. But Purdy didn’t look shorthanded. Not in the least. Tight end George Kittle was back in action despite a quick return from his Achilles injury last year. Receiver Mike Evans looked like the chain-mover, with a touchdown or a first down on all six of his catches. In other words, Evans was everything that they hoped he’d be when they signed him for $42.4 million and three years. Even Deebo Samuel looked young again — like his old 49ers self — with contributions in the passing game (48 receiving yards), running game (12 yards) and on special teams (74 yards). Christian McCaffrey was, of course, outstanding. But it was rookie running back Kaelon Black who was the biggest surprise. He finished with 14 carries for 65 yards. And took the load off McCaffrey at this early phase in the season. In short, the 49ers offense looked awesome. It looked deep. It looked peak Shanahan, with a swath of weapons that should help Purdy play at a really high level — even when facing what everyone had expected to be the NFL’s defense (in L.A.). It looked built to last into January and maybe even February. 2.Jet Lag Hit Both QBs, But Definitely More To Stafford For all the discussion about which team planned their travel correctly, both quarterbacks looked sluggish in the first half. In fact, they both threw brutal interceptions — in the same fashion … on back-to-back drives. Twins! Purdy threw directly at a dropping safety, Quentin Lake, in an attempt for George Kittle, but Lake picked off the throw easily. And then a few plays later, Matthew Stafford floated a ball toward receiver Puka Nacua and Renardo Green backpedaled into position for a pick. You can try all you want to avoid jet lag, but it always wins. That said, Stafford looked worse than Purdy. Stafford aired a few balls so high that they proved uncatchable. He forced a dangerous throw to Davante Adams near the end of the first half. And he looked completely stumped by the 49ers’ pressure, which they generated without having to send many blitzes. For the game, Stafford finished 15 of 25 for 155 yards and an interception. Even Rams head coach Sean McVay looked a little jet-lagged, calling a QB sneak on the goal line on fourth-and-1 in the third quarter. And very much unsurprisingly, Stafford, who is notoriously bad at sneaks, couldn’t convert. On the whole, it felt like the reigning MVP was processing at a slower clip than normal. 3.Trent Williams Killed The Hype Of Myles Garrett's Rams Debut Maybe it wouldn’t hurt to get Aaron Donald into the mix on this defensive line? I thought there would be an embarrassment of riches. I thought the Rams defensive front would be unstoppable. I thought the hype was real. But Myles Garrett finished this game with zero sacks and zero QB hits — even with Purdy dropping back 34 times. Garrett’s pressure total was solid, up to five, per Next Gen Stats. But there’s no way he made the impact that he would’ve hoped. And that’s a real credit to Williams, the 49ers left tackle who was an absolute beast in pass protection against the guy who finished No. 1 in the "NFL 100" rankings. Near the end of the game, however, Netflix’s Tom Pelissero provided an interesting nugget. Garrett had been nursing a knee injury in training camp, which limited his practice reps and — perhaps — affected his conditioning in this game. To make matters worse, he was still dealing with a little pain from the injury. That’ll be something to keep an eye on. 3 1/2. What's Next? There's a downside to the 49ers getting to Australia as early as they did. Now, they’ve got to go home and readjust to Pacific Time. But there’s actually good news. The 49ers will take on the Miami Dolphins, a team that looks like a clear-cut favorite (at least to me) to finish with the No. 1 pick. And then their Week 3 opponent is, frankly, another pushover. The 49ers will take on the Cardinals. So they might lose some sleep as they get their clocks right. But they’re not going to lose any sleep over their game plans. I have no doubt that San Francisco will start this season 3-0. All should be well for when the 49ers host the Broncos in the first week of October in Week 4. The Rams have a Monday night appointment with the Giants in Week 2. Hopefully, their emphasis on not acclimating to the Australian time change will help them feel ready for that matchup, because head coach John Harbaugh has New York feeling good about what the season has in store for the Giants’ young offensive core of quarterback Jaxson Dart, receiver Malik Nabers and running back Cam Skattebo. After this dud, I can’t imagine the Rams will show up with a shortage of energy.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts And Jayden Daniels Enter Pivotal Seasons Ahead Of Week 1 Clash
articles.summary: Here's why this the 2026 regular season is so critical for Commanders QB Jayden Daniels and Eagles QB Jalen Hurts.
articles.body: In the NFL, good vibes are fleeting. Just 19 months ago, the Eagles and Commanders were headed into the offseason feeling like they had world-beaters at quarterback. Philadelphia had just conquered the football world, blowing out the Chiefs in Super Bowl LIX with Jalen Hurts taking home MVP honors. Washington, meanwhile, was fresh off its first NFC Championship Game appearance in over 30 years with rookie phenom Jayden Daniels leading the way. Life was good, and that conference championship game felt like the first installment of the NFL’s next great quarterback rivalry. The 2026 season opener will be the first time Hurts and Daniels have faced off since that playoff game and there’s been a significant vibe shift on both sides of the matchup. Both quarterbacks are coming off frustrating 2025 seasons that may have cast some doubt on their long-term future with their respective teams. Hurts and Daniels will be seeking massive contract extensions in the offseason. At that point, Hurts will have one year left on the extension he signed in 2023, and Daniels will be entering his third offseason, when first-round quarterbacks either sign their first big-money extension or end up in contract purgatory, a la Bryce Young in Carolina. So, the stakes are clear for both quarterbacks in 2026: A bounce-back season will be rewarded with a big payday. But if last year’s struggles bleed over into this season, contract talks might be put on hold. QB Jayden DanielsWashington Commanders The bar for a successful season is lower for Daniels than it is for Hurts, with Washington expected to finish in the bottom half of the NFC East. If the third-year pro can just stay healthy for the full 17-game slate, that will be considered a win. If Daniels stays healthy and rediscovers his 2024 form, Washington will write him a blank check in the spring. It’s just hard to envision a repeat of that magical rookie season given the current state of the Commanders offense. The offensive line was an issue last season and will be worse off in 2026 with star left tackle Laremy Tunsil out indefinitely with a torn triceps. Also, it will be up to first-year offensive coordinator David Blough, who’s just three seasons into his coaching career, to work around that massive weakness. It would be understandable if Daniels doesn’t fully bounce back, but Washington may be reluctant to fork over a top-of-the-market deal for a player coming off two disappointing seasons, especially if more injuries pop up. The Commanders wouldn’t have to move off Daniels, but they’d likely push contract talks into the following offseason, which is typically a bad sign for a first-round quarterback. Daniels had issues targeting the middle of the field in 2025, but it was less about his reluctance to make those throws and more about his inability to complete them. Per Pro Football Focus, his accuracy rate on intermediate throws dropped by nearly 10% compared to his rookie season. There were a lot of poorly placed passes on his 2025 film. But the statistical dip can’t be pinned entirely on Daniels, who was throwing into tighter windows last season. With wide receiver Terry McLaurin out hurt, the Commanders were trotting some abysmal receiving groups out there. It got to a point where tight end Zach Ertz became Daniels’ best option against man coverage. Ertz is still a useful player, but when a 35-year-old is your most reliable option on key passing downs, it’s awfully hard to play quarterback. Daniels’s regression from Year 1 to Year 2 can mostly be explained by his performance against man coverage and the blitz, which are closely linked. Washington didn’t have receivers who could punish a defense for playing aggressively, and Daniels loses accuracy when he’s forced to drive a throw into tight coverage. He’s one of the NFL’s better quarterbacks when throwing with touch in between the lines of a zone defense. He just didn’t get to do it often last season. Washington’s offense should be more equipped to deal with aggressive coverage in 2026. Stefon Diggs, who joined via free agency, was one of the NFL’s most productive receivers against tight man-to-man coverage last season. McClaurin is healthy again. And the team prioritized explosive athletes to fill out the rest of the receiving corps, including third-round rookie Antonio Williams and former first-round pick Treylon Burks. Even with the upgrades, this isn’t a world-beating receiving corps, so Daniels will have to take a step as an intermediate passer to make it work. QB Jalen HurtsPhiladelphia Eagles Last week, Eagles general manager Howie Roseman defended Hurts and denied that the clock is ticking on his time in Philadelphia despite the team’s passing game struggles over the past few seasons. "I think the bottom line for us … is winning football games," Roseman said on a recent appearance on the "Move the Sticks" podcast. "And all [Hurts] does is win football games … for me, the barometer is winning football games." I don’t expect Roseman to get into the nuances of quarterback evaluation during a podcast hit, but that’s a reductive view of Hurts that also suggests his value to the team is directly tied to its winning percentage. If the Eagles have a down year, and the passing game doesn’t improve, will the front office view of Hurts shift? If that’s the case, then it does feel like there’s a lot riding on this season in regard to his future with the team. Supporting talent is less of a concern for Hurts – who is still surrounded by blue-chip players even after the team traded away his top receiver, A.J. Brown – but he’ll also be getting his play calls from an inexperienced offensive coordinator with Sean Mannion coming over from Green Bay. While Hurts is no stranger to OC changes, this is the first time in his NFL career where he’ll have to learn an entirely new offense from the ground up. Mannion is Nick Sirianni’s fifth offensive coordinator in Philly, but it’s the first time he’s gone outside of his coaching tree to make a hire. This won’t be some subtle rebrand. The Eagles offense will be an entirely new thing. Hurts won’t be playing in the shotgun nearly as much and there will be fewer spread formations. It will look more like the 49ers and Rams offenses, with the quarterback under center, condensed formations, and a lot of play-action passing. That’s the hope, at least. In April, ESPN dropped a report on the team’s growing frustration with Hurts’ reluctance to step outside of his comfort zone, which created a lot of the issues that have plagued Philly’s passing game over the past three seasons. Here’s a key excerpt from the report: "He has pushed back on changes that would diversify the scheme, sources said, including when it comes to him going under center more. He has shown a reluctance to let it rip at times, particularly against zone coverage." The report also covered Hurts butting heads with former offensive coordinator Kellen Moore over the use of pre-snap motion. Moore, who’s been calling plays for NFL offenses since 2019, is a big proponent of the tactic but dialed back his usage in 2024 to suit Hurts’ preferences. ESPN also quoted sources close to Hurts who denied those claims, but this season will give us a clear answer. Mannion’s offense is built around all the tactics that are supposedly outside of the quarterback’s comfort zone. This system doesn’t work without pre-snap motion. It doesn’t work without going under center. And it doesn’t work when the quarterback is reluctant to "let it rip" over the middle of the field against zone coverage. Hurts’ reluctance to throw over the middle of the field isn’t just theoretical at this point. Per Next Gen Stats, Hurts targeted the middle third of the field at the league’s lowest rate in 2025. It was the fifth year in a row he’s accomplished that feat. He’s had four different offensive coordinators over that span, so there’s a clear common denominator. My theory: Hurts doesn’t have top-end arm strength but makes up for it with a keen understanding of his own limitations. Hurts avoids the middle of the field for the same reason Jared Goff doesn’t throw on the run: it’s not his game. Making throws into tight zone windows with repeated success isn’t in his wheelhouse and not a winning strategy for him. It can hold back the offense at times, but it limits turnovers. Here’s an example from the Eagles' loss to the Broncos last season. You can see Hurts consider making the stick throw to wide receiver DeVonta Smith between two zone defenders before thinking better of it and settling for an out-of-structure heave downfield. But when the windows are clearer – or the Eagles are in catch-up mode late and turnovers are less of a concern – Hurts will take his shots over the middle. If this scheme change is going to work, one of two things needs to happen: Either Mannion is the second-coming of Shanahan and consistently provides Hurts with clear throwing windows over the middle, or Hurts takes more chances, even if it leads to a small bump to his interception totals. Sunday’s opener will be our first glimpse at the new offenses in Washington and Philadelphia. While it’s important to give these first-year coordinators some grace and give their quarterbacks time to get acclimated to their new digs, the game will provide a perfect stress test for Daniels and Hurts thanks to the defensive matchups on both sides. How will Daniels fare against an Eagles secondary that closes throwing windows as well as any defense in the league? Will Hurts look comfortable going under center and turning his back to the defense on play-action defense against a Washington scheme built around pre-snap disguises and post-snap chaos? The answer to those questions will have ramifications that stretch far beyond the final score on Sunday. They’ll determine how far the Eagles and Commanders can go in 2026 and how much confidence they should have in their franchise quarterbacks beyond this season.

articles.summary: International Sports News: Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury could finally have a new home, with Cardiff’s Principality Stadium emerging as a possible venue for the highly anticipate.
articles.body: Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury could finally have a new home, with Cardiff’s Principality Stadium emerging as a possible venue for the highly anticipated heavyweight clash. The Welsh stadium could host the fight in the early hours of the morning to meet broadcaster Netflix’s demands for its huge US audience.The Welsh government could approve an extension to the stadium’s 10.30pm curfew. A Saturday, November 28 date has reportedly been discussed. Cardiff could provide a compromise after disagreements over staging the fight at Wembley Stadium in London or Madison Square Garden in New York.Principality Stadium emerges as compromise for Anthony Joshua vs Tyson FuryThe Principality Stadium could now be the solution to the long-running venue dispute surrounding Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury.The 80,000-capacity stadium has a retractable roof. That could make it an attractive option for a late-November fight. It also has a strong history of hosting major boxing events.Joe Calzaghe fought Mikkel Kessler at the stadium in 2007. The fight took place at around 2am. That timing could be repeated for Joshua and Fury if the event goes ahead in Cardiff.Boxing dealmaker Turki Al-Sheikh has reportedly been pushing for a 2am start. The timing would help the fight reach viewers in the United States during a more suitable evening slot.Netflix, which is expected to broadcast the contest, had wanted New York as the venue. The US location would have allowed the fight to take place at a more convenient time for American viewers.However, Joshua’s promoter Eddie Hearn has pushed for the fight to remain in the UK. Wembley was viewed as the preferred option. Hearn has reportedly refused to move forward unless the contracts are rewritten with improved financial terms.Wembley’s strict curfew has also caused problems. The stadium has an 11pm limit, making the proposed 2am start difficult.Cardiff could avoid that issue if the Welsh government approves the required extension to the stadium’s current 10.30pm curfew.A press conference could reportedly take place next week, although that depends on approval from the Welsh government.The Welsh Rugby Union is also keen to bring more boxing to the venue.A spokesperson for the organisation said, “We’d be delighted to host this fight. We are very keen to attract more boxing to the stadium, which has a rich history in the sport, enhanced by its closable roof, unrivalled sight lines and unique city-centre location.”Joshua also has previous experience fighting in Cardiff. He defeated Carlos Takam there in 2017 before beating Joseph Parker in the Welsh capital in 2018.However, the fight has remained under pressure because of disagreements between the camps.With Cardiff potentially satisfying the demands of Joshua’s camp, Netflix and Turki Al-Sheikh, the Welsh capital could now provide the compromise needed to finally make Joshua vs Fury happen.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: BS Meter on Connor Hellebuyck, Dylan Larkin, Quinn Hughes and Latest NHL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: NHL training camps open next week, and not a moment too soon for fans after a quiet August with little real hockey news, especially on the trade front.
articles.body:
NHL training camps open next week, and not a moment too soon for fans after a quiet August with little real hockey news, especially on the trade front.

Only three trades occurred in August , none involving established NHL players. The drought ended on Sept. 1, when the Nashville Predators shipped winger Luke Evangelista to the New Jersey Devils for two draft picks.

That move could awaken a slumbering trade market as NHL general managers evaluate their rosters before the puck officially drops on the 2026-27 regular season on Sept. 29.

Most of the recent trade speculation involved notable stars like Winnipeg Jets goalie Connor Hellebucyk, Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin, and Minnesota Wild defenseman Quinn Hughes. They were among the players featured in our NHL Trade Targets Big Board for September 2026 .

Could one of those stars be moved this month? Follow along as we deploy our trusty BS Meter to separate fact from fiction.

Will the Boston Bruins Trade Mason Lohrei?

Trade rumors dogged Mason Lohrei through most of last season and into the early weeks of the offseason. That conjecture landed the 25-year-old Boston Bruins defenseman at No. 7 on our July NHL Trade Block Big Board .

The speculation died away as the summer progressed. On Aug. 22, Lohrei told The Boston Globe 's Jim McBride that he was looking forward to the challenge of earning a full-time spot on the Bruins' blue line after being a healthy scratch for several regular-season and playoff games in 2025-26.

RG Media's James Murphy reported on Sept. 7 that multiple league sources claimed Lohrei was again drawing interest in the trade market. He said Lohrei was in play last season when the Bruins attempted to acquire Rasmus Andersson from the Calgary Flames before he was traded to the Vegas Golden Knights.

Lohrei is in the final season of a two-year contract with an average annual value of $3.2 million. He's slated to become a restricted free agent next summer with arbitration rights.

The Bruins may not be shopping Lohrei, but they could be open to trade offers. They also have a crowded blue line this season, which could make him a trade chip to address other roster issues, such as depth at center.

Are the St. Louis Blues Interested in Alexander Nikishin?

Trade rumors have swirled around Alexander Nikishin since June following reports that the Carolina Hurricanes were considering whether to re-sign or peddle him. The speculation reached a point where a trade seemed certain, earning the 24-year-old defenseman the No. 4 spot on our August Trade Targets Big Board .

Nikishin is a restricted free agent after completing his entry-level contract and is ineligible to sign an offer sheet because he lacks the minimum number of NHL games. He had a promising debut last season with 11 goals and 33 points, but his role and playing time were reduced during the Hurricanes' Stanley Cup run.

The conjecture died down during a quiet August in the NHL trade market. However, persistent rumblings have linked Nikishin to the St. Louis Blues since July. Jeremy Rutherford of The Athletic first reported that the Blues were believed to be interested in the young blueliner.

On Sept. 1, Rutherford boldly predicted that the Blues would acquire and sign Nikishin. He claimed the 6'3", 218-pound left-shot blueliner was the type of defenseman that general manager Alexander Steen was looking for.

The Hurricanes could re-sign Nikishin or perhaps peddle him to another club. Nevertheless, the rumors linking him to the Blues haven't gone away. It wouldn't be surprising if he ends up in St. Louis on a bridge contract.

Since his trade request was reported in early June, Dylan Larkin has been a fixture in the offseason rumor mill. The 30-year-old Detroit Red Wings center sits at No. 2 on our NHL Trade Targets Big Board for September 2026 . His request is currently in limbo as the Red Wings search for a new general manager.

Larkin is signed through 2030-31 with an average annual value of $8.7 million. He has a full no-movement clause, but will waive it for the Minnesota Wild, Florida Panthers, and Vegas Golden Knights. The Dallas Stars are also rumored as a possible landing spot.

However, Larkin's preferred destinations lack the salary cap space and tradeable assets to acquire him. Some observers suggest he must widen his list if he hopes to be traded before the regular season begins, assuming the Red Wings have hired a new GM by then.

On Aug. 28, NHL Network's Mike Johnson suggested the Montréal Canadiens as a trade destination if Larkin wants to play for a Stanley Cup contender. He noted that the Canadiens are loaded with young talent to be a contender for several years. They can draw on some of it to make a tempting offer to the Red Wings.

Larkin's list of landing spots is all American-based teams. He's unlikely to join the Canadiens or any other Canadian franchises. If he has to widen his trade list, it probably won't include clubs north of the border.

Will the Minnesota Wild Trade Quinn Hughes If They Can't Re-Sign Him?

The uncertainty over Quinn Hughes' future with the Minnesota Wild earned him the No. 13 spot on our September NHL Trade Targets Big Board . As training camp approaches without a contract extension for the 26-year-old superstar defenseman, trade speculation continues to brew about his future.

On Aug. 31, Wild general manager Bill Guerin acknowledged that defenseman Cale Makar's record-setting contract with the Colorado Avalanche set a bar for Hughes. However, he also said Hughes was a different personality who wanted different things out of life. "Who knows what he's gonna want in the end," Guerin said.

NHL insider Frank Seravalli told Sportsnet that he felt the Wild should sign Hughes soon or move on from him. He suggested the New Jersey Devils as a potential trade or free-agent destination, citing that Hughes' brothers, Jack and Luke, play for the Devils.

The Athletic's Michael Russo reported that Guerin remained confident he can get Hughes re-signed. However, while the blueliner still believes in the Wild and praised Guerin and the team, he won't be rushed into signing an extension, saying he wants to make the right decision for everyone involved.

The longer Hughes goes without an extension, the more questions will be raised about whether he really wants to stay in Minnesota. If his reluctance stretches into the New Year, Guerin could feel the pressure to move him before the March 1 trade deadline.

Could the Winnipeg Jets Have Difficulty Trading Connor Hellebuyck?

Perched atop our September NHL Trade Targets Big Board , Connor Hellebucyk's days with the Winnipeg Jets appear to be numbered. He revealed last month that he requested a trade this spring and still believes it would be best for him and his family to move to another NHL city.

Hellebuyck, 33, should attract plenty of interest in the trade market. An elite goaltender, he's the league's only active three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also won the Hart Memorial Trophy in 2024-25 and backstopped Team USA to gold in the 2026 Winter Olympics.

While Hellebuyck has a full no-movement clause , Chris Johnston of The Athletic reported on Aug. 27 that he's willing to waive it for "a variety of teams". His colleague, Pierre LeBrun, reported that the Carolina Hurricanes, Buffalo Sabres, and Utah Mammoth are among the possibilities.

However, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman told NHL Network last Friday that the trade options open to the Jets earlier this summer are no longer available . He also noted that some players who may have been available before July 1 may no longer be because their no-trade clauses had changed.

Friedman believed the Florida Panthers were interested in Hellebuyck but used most of their trade capital to acquire Brady Tkachuk. The Jets discussed a deal with the Buffalo Sabres, but Friedman said a disagreement about swapping 2026 first-round picks scuttled that plan.

articles.title: Tennessee Titans' Calvin Ridley: 'Don't listen to the noise outside'
articles.summary: Calvin Ridley breaks his silence on the Tennessee Titans offense as he prepares for the season opener against the Jets.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans returned to the practice field on Thursday to prepare for their season opener against the New York Jets on Sunday, and multiple players met with the media afterward.

One of those players, wide receiver Calvin Ridley , has been rather quiet throughout training camp, although he is the veteran in the room. That changed on Thursday, when he opened up about what he is seeing as he enters his third season in Nashville.

"I like everything (coaches) have been doing. They all have a lot of experience, especially with (OC Brian) Daboll being in our room, coach (Robert) Saleh being the head coach – and all of them being head coaches before. They're very calm. I have a lot of confidence in us. We've looked good, so just don't listen to the noise outside; just play our football."

Ridley has been quiet both on and off the field throughout preseason and training camp, as he works his way back from the leg injury that ended his 2024 season early. Now, after the offseason additions of Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson, he looks to take a new role on the offense and is no longer the Titans' most important threat on the outside. Something that could pay dividends as the season wears on.

articles.title: Julian Etse signs professional contract
articles.summary: Eintracht Frankfurt have handed the 20-year-old defender a professional contract. Etse arrived in Frankfurt from SSV Ulm 1846 in the summer.The 1.92 metre-ta...
articles.body:
Eintracht Frankfurt have handed the 20-year-old defender a professional contract. Etse arrived in Frankfurt from SSV Ulm 1846 in the summer.

The 1.92 metre-tall defender underwent his footballing education at VfL Bochum from 2015 to 2018. In total he made 59 competitive appearances for VfL's U17 and U19 sides in the Bundesliga youth leagues, scoring five goals.

The centre-back moved to 3. Liga outfit Ulm in summer 2025. After four appearances in the first half of the season, Etse spent the rest of the campaign on loan at TSV Steinbach Haiger in the Regionalliga Südwest. He quickly established himself as a first-team regular for the Hesse club, featuring in 12 of a possible 14 matches. Then in summer 2026, he joined Eintracht.

The German of Ghanaian heritage has made four appearances for the Eintracht U21s so far in the current Regionalliga Südwest season. He only missed the opening game against KSV Hessen Kassel because he was taking part in the first team's pre-season training camp in Grassau. Etse also led the Eagles as captain in the meetings against SV Stuttgarter Kickers and VfR Aalen.

Sporting director Timmo Hardung said: "Julian has taken a big step forward in the last few months. With his size, his physicality and his mentality, he has exciting attributes for his position as a centre-back. By giving him a professional contract, we're now providing the foundation for Julian to continue developing at a high level. He'll continue to play an important role in our U21s and gain valuable game time there, which is vital for his development. We'll monitor him closely and give him the opportunity to work towards the level and the requirements of professional football."

articles.title: Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz make Solheim history with 5-0 record
articles.summary: Korda and Copuz have anchored a foursomes revolution for the red, white and blue.
articles.body:
CROMVOIRT, Netherlands — When stats guru Justin Ray first starts to put potential pairings together, he takes the names and faces away and simply looks at the data. Allisen Corpuz's incredible accuracy off the tee, coupled with Nelly Korda's world-class approach play, seemed like a no-brainer to Ray. Add in Corpuz's cool-headed, comfortable approach to the spotlight, and it was a partnership 2023 U.S. captain Stacy Lewis was keen to put in play.

Now the first duo to win five consecutive matches in Solheim Cup history, Korda and Copuz have anchored a foursomes revolution for the red, white and blue.

"It's like having an ace at the top of your rotation in major league baseball," said Ray, who Lewis first brought on to help with the 2023 matches in Spain. It marked the first time the U.S. had ever used a stats-based system to help with the Solheim Cup , a practice that's been done for years at the Ryder Cup .

After the pair went 4-0 in foursomes in 2023 and 2024, Angela Stanford didn't have too much to consider.

"I feel like the whole world knew that they were coming," she said after putting them out first for Friday foursomes at Bernardus Golf.

Anna Nordqvist sent out her best to take them on in Charley Hull and Lottie Woad, two top-10 players playing together for the first time. After the Englishwomen birdied the first hole to go 1 up, it was USA the rest of the way. Korda and Corpuz dispatched the Euros, 4 and 3, with a solid performance.

"Honestly, I enjoy playing with her so much," said Korda, who improves her overall record to 11-5-1.

Corpuz and Korda become the second Solheim tandem to earn five points, joining Laura Davies and Alison Nicholas, who have a 5-4-0 record.

On the men's side, Arnold Palmer and Gardner Dickinson are the only players in Ryder Cup history to win all five matches they played together from 1967-1971, according to Elias Sports Bureau.

Corpuz, who, like Korda, is a U.S. Women's Open champion, improves her overall record to 6-2-1.

"Every time we even get to play practice rounds with [Korda] – I feel like that's not something we really do on a regular tournament week – so just to be able to see the way she practices," said Corpuz of what she's learned about the world No. 1. "... everything that she does is just so elite. I think just, personality-wise, like she's also really easy to be around. I'm pretty calm and she is as well, so I think there's a good energy match there."

Beth Ann Nichols is a senior writer for Golfweek covering the LPGA and all things women's golf. Follow her on X/Twitter (@GolfweekNichols).

articles.title: ‘A uniquely American job’: What it takes to be a big-time college quarterback
articles.summary: A select, small quarterback fraternity can appreciate the opportunity, pressure and glory college football presents.
articles.body: Arch Manning was talking about his golf game, replying to a throwaway question at Texas’ SEC football media day about how he blows off steam in the offseason. The Longhorns quarterback said he’d been hitting the links regularly on the weekends, tagging along most recently with a buddy who was a member at Barton Creek Country Club to play the Ben Crenshaw-designed course in Austin. The driver, Manning said, had been working particularly well, so well that the 10-handicap golfer had just broke 80 for the first time. This was back in July, less than a week before the Longhorns would head into full preseason workouts, and Manning admitted that his golf days were numbered. “I’m going to have to stop here in a week or so until about February,” he said, A reporter interrupted before Manning could finish his thought. “Not January?” he asked. Manning looked quizzically at him. “Whenever the season ends,” Manning replied, to which the reporter responded, “The season ends at the end of January.” Manning smiled. “Right, so I’ll be playing golf again in February.’’ This is what it is to be a college quarterback, where simple exchanges have hidden messages – or worse, landmines to avoid – and to speak is to risk having your every word parsed. It is chronic accountability coupled with crippling responsibility. It is to be the big man on campus, until you become the biggest loser. It is to be both Fernando Mendoza, Heisman winner, and Alberto Mendoza, recruited-over backup forced to transfer. It is to possess a strong arm, a sharp mind, a rhinoceros’ thick skin and a goldfish’s memory. “People say good things about you when you win and bad things about you when you lose,” Ohio State signal-caller Julian Sayin said during the Buckeyes’ Big Ten media day. Sayin stopped to smile. “Actually, sometimes they say bad things about you when you win, too.” On one hand, it is fair to ponder: Who would want such a job? But on the other, is the truth. Who wouldn’t? In the hierarchy of sporting alpha males, there is no one higher than quarterback. They are the varsity jacket-wearing, high school heartthrobs and the NFL ad pitchmen, the players kids clamor to be and who companies want to associate with. Lost in the fanfare is the very delicate balance they are asked to walk between fame and infamy, adulation and abuse, but the allure makes it hard not to want to take the walk. “It is a uniquely American job,” says author and ESPN.com writer Seth Wickersham, who sought to understand the position of quarterback in his book, “American Kings.” “You wear all of these hats that no other sport requires you to wear. Amateur psychologist, spokesperson, breathtaking a**hole, all of these things you have to be and not everybody has it and to this day, I don’t think anybody knows where it comes from.” A high-profile showdown in Austin No doubt in part aided by the availability of NIL money, this year’s crop of college signal-callers is especially abundant. Of the top 20 players with odds to win the Heisman Trophy by BetMGM, only two party-crashing wide receivers, Jeremiah Smith (Ohio State) and Malachi Toney (University of Miami), break up the glut of quarterbacks. They all arrived via different paths. Some took the one less traveled – Trinidad Chambliss went from Division II Ferris State to Ole Miss. Others took the scenic route. Miami’s Darian Mensah started at Tulane, transferred to Duke and then hightailed it to join the Hurricanes this year. And one took a direct snap – BYU’s Bear Bachmeier became the Cougars’ first freshman to start behind center in school history when he debuted against Portland State last season. This weekend, two – Manning and Sayin – will go head-to-head in a top-5 rematch of a game that ought to serve as a quarterback cautionary tale. After the Buckeyes topped the Longhorns, 14-7, in 2025, Manning was tabbed an automatic flop and Sayin destined to chart the path to another national title for OSU. Neither, of course, held true. Manning got better over time, putting the bow on his season with 376 total yards and four touchdowns against Michigan in the Citrus Bowl. “I think … what he got put through probably would have melted or destroyed 99% of people in his shoes,” Manning’s coach Steve Sarkisian said. “All he did was stay consistent and true to who he was, which was to continue to work hard, continue to be a great teammate, try to get better, and he did.” Sayin, in the meantime, struggled to the finish. He was bumpy in a win against Michigan and then came up short in the Big Ten championship game against Indiana and in the first-round playoff loss against Miami. “Julian Sayin has a different look in his eye,” his coach, Ryan Day, said. “He had great success last year. Won his first start ever, home against Texas, top five matchup. Won our rivalry game in the sideways snow. Came up short at the end of the year. We all did. When you look in his eye now, you see a different person, a different body. He’s worked.” Whether Manning comes into his own or Sayin shows a new glimmer remains to be seen. But it won’t stop the conjecture before the game – or the referendums after it. “Everyone has an opinion, and people are paid to talk in the media,” Manning said. “There’s nothing you can do. I’m controlling the controllables, but it probably lights a little bit of a fire in me.” All the smoke Which is, of course, one of the great separators of quarterbacks from mere mortals. They want the smoke. For all that fans project on them – assuming they are the smartest, best looking, standard of masculinity – they bring their own set of necessary traits to the table, too. A degree of arrogance is required for the position, a willingness to absorb the spotlight partnered with the certainty that you are built to handle it. “As a kid, you grow up and you dream of being in that situation,” said John Mateer, Oklahoma’s starter. Which, really, every kid does. Who hasn’t hustled out into the backyard to mimic their sports heroes? But it is one thing to make believe; it is altogether a different story to do the job and do it well. Wickersham spent more than a year writing his book and cultivated the background from a sportswriting life spent observing QBs. He once dreamed of being one himself, which is what ignited the curiosity. He talked to, among others, John Elway, Steve Young and Warren Moon, while also traipsing around youth camps and talking to kids tabbed as the next insert-name-of-great-QB-here. He believes quarterbacks can be both curated and created. Some have innate talent that is naturally honed and directed. A kid with a gun for an arm and physical gifts is directed behind center much like the wily speedster heads to the wide receiver or defensive back group. Others, for certain, are incubated by gridiron versions of cheer moms, who shuffle their sons around in search of stardom. But both, he says, eventually develop a brash confidence that allows them master the position. Wickersham says, with only the slightest of chuckles, that every quarterback is something of a sociopath and likens them to politicians in the middle of a race. They require bad news filters and chronic reassurance and, contrary to the arrogance required, also have a high degree of insecurity. He even chronicles Tom Brady’s love life evolution – from dating Tara Reid to marrying Giselle Bündchen – as the evidence of the quarterback mindset. “That’s not a mistake,” Wickersham says. “The quarterback, he can’t not dominate things.” The college football microscope The college game is a curious fishbowl. It is at once not nearly as big as the NFL and yet somehow the spotlight can feel even more glaring. It is a new experience, for starters, with most players getting their first foray into stardom, which can be undercut by at least an attempt at campus normalcy. They walk among us, if you will. Manning has said that often, while walking to class, he’d call his mom, Ellen, so as to avoid either the finger-pointing or the picture requests. Manning, of course, was born for this. The grandson of Archie and nephew of Peyton and Eli, he is next in line in the first family of football. Before he threw a pass, he starred in a national commercial. Not playing was not an option. Asked what he might do if he couldn’t play a sport, Manning looks genuinely perplexed, as if a life without sport had never crossed his mind. Likely because it hadn’t. “Would he be who he is if he was in a different family?” Wickersham says. “I mean, probably not, right?” What’s interesting is that, despite all that life prep, Manning’s transition to starter was bumpy. His overall passing efficiency rating for the 2025 season was 144.92, 42nd nationally and seventh in the SEC. Meanwhile, Chambliss started his career at Ferris, a small school in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Though the program is good – the Bulldogs have won four national titles – there’s no national TV deal. Top Taggart Field seats 6,200. No one knew who he was, really. After transferring to Ole Miss, he was designated Austin Simmons’ backup – until Simmons got hurt. Suddenly, there was Chambliss under center against Arkansas, in front of 65,000 screaming Rebel fans. He threw for more than 400 yards and three touchdowns against the Razorbacks. He started this season ranked as the No. 1 quarterback in the SEC – ahead of Georgia’s Gunner Stockton and Sam Leavitt at LSU, both four-star prospects and Alabama’s Keelon Russell, the No. 2 prospect in his class. “It’s been a crazy ride,” Chambliss said. “I tend not to really look at any of the rankings. I know they have no influence on my team and what our goals are and what we know in our facility. But yeah, I mean, it’s cool they have me ranked that way.” A special fraternity Mateer bumped into Terry Bradshaw at a Dallas-area card show this off season. The two connected via the rarefied air of their profession. Only 22, Mateer was born nearly two decades after Bradshaw retired. He knew him as a Fox TV analyst, not as a four-time Super Bowl winner. Last season, Mateer broke a bone in his throwing hand in September and, though he returned quickly, was not nearly himself. The injury played with his head as much as his game, robbing him of his confidence and physicality. Oklahoma went 2-2 in October, with Mateer only completing 58% of his passes. He says he watches those game films and cringes. So, when he did some digging on Bradshaw, he learned not just about his success but his style of play – he had a cannon for an arm but was known just as much for his fearlessness – and Mateer grew intrigued. He found some old film and started watching. “Terry Bradshaw, y’all, you’re not going to believe it,” Mateer says as if he found a secret sauce. “The way he makes plays and throws the ball around, it’s old school,” he said of Bradshaw. “You take some of the old-school stuff and add it to your game – not a lot of people are going to expect that.” In last week’s season opener, albeit against UTEP, he threw for 225 yards and three touchdowns. Watching from the sideline in a Boomer red shirt and a cowboy hat was Bradshaw, the past watching the future, understanding and appreciating the opportunity, the pressure and the glory as only someone in the small quarterback fraternity can.

articles.title: Hull City new signing Sorba Thomas escapes deadly accident after terrifying $216,000 Land Rover car crash in residential area near training ground
articles.summary: International Sports News: Hull City have confirmed that new signing Sorba Thomas escaped without injury after his Land Rover Defender flipped onto its roof near the club’s trai.
articles.body: Hull City have confirmed that new signing Sorba Thomas escaped without injury after his Land Rover Defender flipped onto its roof near the club’s training ground. Pictures from the scene showed the luxury vehicle upside down on Millhouse Wood Lane in Cottingham on Friday morning.The 27-year-old Wales international was reportedly on his way to training when the crash happened. Emergency services attended the scene, while a Hull City staff member, understood to be manager Sergej Jakirovic, was also pictured at the location. The club later reassured supporters that Thomas was “completely unscathed” after the frightening incident.Sorba Thomas escapes injury after Land Rover crashHull City confirmed Sorba Thomas was involved in the road traffic accident near their Cottingham training ground. The club said the winger suffered no injuries despite his vehicle ending up on its roof.A statement from Hull City read, “Hull City is relieved to confirm that Sorba Thomas is unharmed following a road traffic accident near to the club’s Cottingham training ground. The club is aware of images of Sorba’s car circulating on social media and can reassure supporters that he has sustained no injuries and emerged from his vehicle completely unscathed.”Humberside Police also confirmed that officers and emergency services were at the scene. The crash happened at around 9am on Friday, September 11, 2026.Police said, “Officers and emergency services are currently in attendance following reports of a road traffic collision on Milllhouse Woods Lane, Cottingham at around 9am on Friday, 11 September 2026. The road remains closed and motorists are advised to avoid the area to allow emergency services to operate effectively.”Images shared on social media showed Thomas’ Land Rover Defender overturned on the residential road. The vehicle also appeared to have suffered damage, including smashed glass.A Hull City staff member was seen at the scene. He was reportedly manager Sergej Jakirovic, who had spoken positively about Thomas just one day earlier.Thomas joined Hull from Stoke City on transfer deadline day for a reported £10.5 million ($14.18m). The Wales international made the move after an impressive season with Stoke, where he was named the club’s Player of the Year.He scored 10 goals and provided 13 assists in all competitions last season.Thomas has made two appearances for Hull since completing his transfer. He came off the bench during the club’s 0-0 Premier League draw with Aston Villa. He also started the 1-0 Carabao Cup defeat against Sunderland.Hull are scheduled to face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon. The Tigers have made an impressive start to life in the Premier League after winning promotion through the Championship play-offs.They defeated Manchester United and Coventry before drawing with Aston Villa. Hull currently sit third in the table, making Thomas’ availability an important boost for Jakirovic.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Sophie Cunningham marked her 30th birthday with a bold lakeside photo set, giving fans a closer look at her celebratory weekend in Missouri. The Indiana Fever guard shared the images on Instagram during the WNBA's break, posing in a colorful strapless bikini with a relaxed vacation look. Her caption added a playful twist, linking the birthday celebration to one of television's most recognizable ranch characters.The post came several weeks after Cunningham's Aug. 16 birthday, giving her time to celebrate with family and friends at the Lake of the Ozarks in Osage Beach, Missouri. Along with the beachside photos, Cunningham also offered a glimpse into the personality behind her confident public image, while a separate podcast appearance showed she has bigger ideas for the WNBA's future.Sophie Cunningham celebrates 30th birthday in tiny strapless bikiniSophie Cunningham celebrated her 30th birthday with a colorful bikini look during a weekend trip to the Lake of the Ozarks. The Indiana Fever guard shared a multi-image Instagram carousel in mid-September, posting photos from the gathering with family and friends during the WNBA's FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup break.Cunningham wore a tiny bandeau-style bikini top featuring a colorful abstract print and a tied knot detail in the center. Matching high-cut bottoms highlighted her athletic build, while an orange trucker-style cap and gold necklace completed the outfit.The setting also had a personal connection for Cunningham. She grew up in Columbia, Missouri, and has family ties to a ranch in the state. Her birthday celebration near the Lake of the Ozarks therefore offered more than a typical getaway backdrop.Her caption gave the photos their most playful detail. Cunningham wrote, “my wish is to be Beth Dutton when I grow up.”Beth Dutton, played by Kelly Reilly on Yellowstone, is known for her sharp tongue, fierce loyalty and intense personality. Cunningham's reference fit the Missouri setting and her ranch connection, while fans also picked up on the humor behind the comparison.Sophie Cunningham wants to become the next WNBA commissionerCunningham's birthday post showed her playful side, but she has also made it clear she has strong views about where the WNBA should go next.During the debut episode of her new podcast, “No Hesitation,” Cunningham was asked by co-host Drew Hanlen if she would consider becoming the league's next commissioner. Let me tell you that.”The idea could become relevant sooner than a casual podcast answer might suggest. WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert has announced plans to retire at the end of the 2026 season, setting up a search for new leadership at a major point in the league's growth.Cunningham also had a clear answer when Hanlen asked what she would change first.“Honestly, the first thing I would do is make sure that every team legit has a functional practice facility,” she said. “There are teams in the WNBA, which this is, we are supposed to be, not supposed, we are the best league in the entire world, that they, we're, there are people practicing at like YMCAs. They're sharing a court by a curtain when there's like YMCA youth camps going on one side and a team practicing on the other.”Right now, Cunningham's attention is still on helping Indiana finish its season strongly, but her podcast comments suggest she is thinking beyond her playing career too.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ricky Hatton’s mother recalls emotional final hug just three days before boxing champion’s death by suicide at 46
articles.summary: International Sports News: Ricky Hatton’s mother has recalled the final hug she shared with her son, just three days before he died by suicide aged 46. Carol Hatton said she mad.
articles.body: Ricky Hatton’s mother has recalled the final hug she shared with her son, just three days before he died by suicide aged 46. Carol Hatton said she made an unplanned visit to his gym in Hyde after the pair had been involved in an argument.Carol and Ricky’s father, Ray, have spoken publicly for the first time since the former world champion’s death on September 14 last year. They urged people to tell their loved ones they care about them before it is too late. The couple are also calling for a statue of Ricky to be built in Manchester.Carol Hatton remembers her son Ricky Hatton’s final daysCarol Hatton said she visited Ricky Hatton after seeing his car outside the gym. She had not planned to go inside, but decided to see him.The family had been trying to repair their relationship after years of difficulties. Ricky had previously been estranged from his parents for about a decade. He had also spoken openly about his struggles with drug and alcohol addiction and had survived earlier suicide attempts.Carol told ITV News, “I pulled up on the car park because I saw his car. He asked if everything was okay. I said “yeah, everything’s fine”. I said I’d like to see a bit more of him.”She said the meeting ended with a meaningful embrace.“I’m so glad (I got to see him) because nobody knows when it’s the last time you’re going to see somebody”, she added.During the visit, Ricky told his mother that he wanted to see his father the following week. However, he died three days later.Ray said the experience had made him think about how people show love to their families. He encouraged parents, especially fathers, to speak openly to their sons.“You tell your grandkids how much you love them, you tell your wife how much you love them but I think, especially with men, don’t ever be afraid of getting hold of your son and telling him you love him”, Ray said.Ricky’s relationship with his parents had been damaged by a long-running dispute over money and family contact. Despite the disagreement, Carol and Ray were allowed to see his daughter, Millie, for a period.The situation became worse after Ricky’s girlfriend, Jennifer, was not invited to a Christmas Day gathering. Months later, Ricky received letters from his parents’ lawyers about contact with Millie.In a 2013 interview with the Manchester Evening News, Ricky said, “I replied to my parents, through solicitors, and said we did not want them to have contact with Millie.”He also described the family dispute as “a mess” and “bitter and horrible”. The conflict later led to a physical fight between Ricky and his father in a car park.Ray said he had been angry about “all that stuff you’ve written about your mum in that solicitor’s letter”. He punched Ricky, who then hit back before Ray drove away.Despite their painful history, Carol and Ray said they are trying to move forward while keeping Ricky’s memory alive. Carol said they would continue “remembering him and loving him”.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Dylan Larkin Stripped of Red Wings Captaincy After Requesting Trade During NHL Free Agency
articles.summary: With no movement on his trade request, Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin will report to training camp. Except he won't be a captain anymore.
articles.body:
With no movement on his trade request, Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin will report to training camp. Except he won't be a captain anymore.

Larkin and the Red Wings announced Friday he intends to be with the team when camp opens next week, but the club's statement also noted they intend to open the 2026-27 season without a captain.

Larkin reportedly requested a trade in June, weeks before the start of free agency. There was no indication at that point a deal was anywhere close.

Earlier this week, The Athletic's Michael Russo said on KFAN in Minnesota that Larkin wasn't in attendance for Detroit's captain's practice and he still hoped to be traded. The Minnesota Wild were specifically cited as one of his preferred landing spots.

It's no secret the Wild have been shopping for a top-line center. Russo reported in June they made a "huge" offer to the Ottawa Senators for Brady Tkachuk, but he was ultimately traded to the Florida Panthers.

According to Russo , Minnesota's offer for Tkachuk was the equivalent of four first-round draft picks.

Larkin's trade value is interesting to parse out right now. He is four years older than Tkachuk, but he is under team control for five seasons with salaries of $8.7 million through 2030-31. Tkachuk only has two years remaining on his current deal.

The Red Wings officially named Larkin team captain in January 2021, making him the 37th player in franchise history to hold the title. He had been an alternate captain since the 2018-19 season.

A first-round pick in the 2014 draft, Larkin has spent his entire career in Detroit. He ranks 10th in franchise history in goals scored (276) and has recorded at least 30 goals in five consecutive seasons.

Red Wings players are scheduled to report to camp on Sept. 17. They will open the regular season on Oct. 2 against the New York Rangers.

Hull City winger Sorba Thomas ⁠⁠escaped “completely ⁠⁠unscathed” when he was involved in a crash near ⁠⁠their training ground, his Premier League club said on Friday.

British media reported that his car ended up on its roof on Friday morning in the village of Cottingham in the East Riding of Yorkshire. Images of his upturned car with shattered glass on a narrow ‌‌street went viral on social media.

“Hull City is relieved to confirm that Sorba Thomas is unharmed following a road traffic accident near to ⁠⁠the club’s Cottingham training ⁠⁠ground,” the club said in a statement .

“The club is aware of images of ⁠⁠Sorba’s car circulating on social media and ⁠⁠can reassure supporters ⁠⁠that he has sustained no injuries and emerged from his vehicle completely unscathed.”

Thomas, 27, joined newly-promoted Hull City from second-tier Championship club Stoke City on the transfer deadline day earlier this month.

The Wales international has made two appearances for Hull, ‌‌who are third in the league standings after three games and visit ‌‌Chelsea on Saturday.
