articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 1 Fades & Busts: Terry McLaurin, Christian Watson among players to consider avoiding
articles.summary: Matt Okada takes you through the 6 players he's fading in Week 1 for fantasy football.
articles.body:
Welcome to the first of many weekly columns spotlighting the fantasy football fades of the week! I am your host, Matt Okada, and I'll be bringing you half a dozen potential busts each and every Friday, from now until the fantasy playoffs.

As a note, just because a player earns a "fade" or "bust" designation doesn't automatically mean they should be benched — it depends on the rest of your roster or the options on your waiver wire. But you can expect them to fall short of expectations (when I get them right). I include a "What to Do" section for every player to help with that.

Without further ado, here is my list for Week 1 of the 2025 season.

This week, the Chiefs and their fans got the good news that Patrick Mahomes is expected to start Monday night ... but that's not necessarily good news for his fantasy managers. It'll be his first game since his major knee injury back in September ... and it comes against the Denver Broncos.

Mahomes has played Denver four times in the three seasons since Vance Joseph took over as defensive coordinator. Mahomes hasn't hit 18 fantasy points in any of those four outings and has averaged just 13.2 PPG in total, with three TD passes, four interceptions, 64 QB pressures and 12 sacks. He finished outside the top 10 quarterbacks in fantasy each of the last three times that he faced his division rival ... and all of this history comes before tearing multiple knee ligaments, having surgery and rehabbing for just nine months. Mahomes will almost certainly be less than 100% this weekend, and that's a recipe for concern against one of the most dangerous defenses in the league. When healthy and taking on a middle-of-the-road opponent, Mahomes is excellent for fantasy — but on Monday, I'd consider him well outside QB1 range.

What to do ❓ Unless you're in a 2QB league, there are almost certainly streaming options worth playing over Mahomes. Guys like Jared Goff, Baker Mayfield and Kyler Murray are easy decisions, and even Tyler Shough and Bo Nix (in the same game) would be preferred. Don't be surprised if he finishes closer to QB20 than QB10 (or certainly QB1).

I've been touting Tuten as one of the biggest bust candidates in all of fantasy this offseason, so it should not come as a surprise to see him crack this column in Week 1 against Cleveland. As it seems much of the fantasy community is finally starting to realize, Tuten was crowned as the RB1 in Jacksonville far too quickly after Travis Etienne Jr.'s departure. Tuten is a fourth-round pick who was hit-or-miss as a rookie, and the Jaguars immediately signed Chris Rodriguez Jr. to compete with Tuten back in March. Notably, Rodriguez was better than Tuten in a number of deeper metrics in 2025, including rush yards before and after contact per carry and explosive run rate (which is supposed to be Tuten's strength).

Then, reports out of training camp repeatedly suggested that the backfield would be more of a committee, with Rodriguez allegedly favored in short yardage, goal-line and two-minute situations.

Despite all of this, Tuten continued to be one of the darlings of the fantasy draft community up until maybe the past week or so, when Rodriguez was listed as a co-starter on the official depth chart, and the reality began to finally set in. I'd nearly guarantee that Tuten will not see the 17 touches per game that Etienne shouldered last season, and I'd frankly be less surprised to see that number end up in the single digits. Rodriguez will also be a major threat to vulture touchdowns all season long and will be my preferred play in games Jacksonville is heavily favored ... like it is against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday.

Tuten will have good games in 2026, and there might even be several you can start him for with confidence, but not in Week 1.

What to do ❓ You likely drafted Tuten as a low-end RB2, so here's hoping you have an alternate to play in the RB2 slot or in your FLEX. If you can, try to bench him for at least this first week to get a sense for the snap and touch distribution in Duval. Names worth playing ahead of him include Jaylen Warren, Tony Pollard, Bucky Irving and possibly even MarShawn Lloyd (though I don't love playing him either).

If you had RJ Harvey down the stretch last season, loved his fantasy output and drafted him again in 2026, hoping for an encore ... you might want to temper expectations. Yes, the second-round pick out of UCF was a top-20 running back from Week 11 on last year, with double-digit touches in every outing and six total touchdowns. But that also coincided with the season-ending injury to J.K. Dobbins, which opened a door for Harvey that had been tightly shut the first 10 weeks. Prior to Dobbins' departure, Harvey had averaged just 8.7 fantasy points per game and seen more than seven carries just once. In fact, his already iffy fantasy output was inflated by four receiving touchdowns across a six-week stretch — Harvey scored just once through the air after taking over as the starter in Week 11.

And, of course, Dobbins is back and healthy for the start of the 2026 season, after signing a two-year, $16 million contract with the Broncos in March. Unsurprisingly, the unofficial depth chart lists Dobbins as the starter over Harvey, and we haven't even mentioned the added presence of exciting rookie Jonah Coleman, who made my All-Sleeper Team a week ago. And to top it all off, Denver is facing the Chiefs defense in Kansas City — never a friendly proposition — and has a bottom-eight lower implied total on the week (20.5). Harvey was just okay in two games against Kansas City as the lead back last year, averaging 11.3 points per game in half-PPR. Now the No. 2 (at best) in a potentially three-headed backfield, I'd expect less from the second-year back on Monday night.

What to do ❓ Sit Harvey if at all possible. It should be plenty doable outside of very deep leagues, as you can honestly pivot to either Panthers back, either Vikings back, either Commanders back, Chris Rodriguez Jr., Tyler Allgeier and others ahead of Harvey.

If this was Week 1 of the 2025 season, after the year Terry McLaurin had in 2024, this would sound patently absurd. He scored 13 touchdowns and was the WR6 overall two years ago ... but he scored just three touchdowns, missed seven games and was just the WR35 in points per game last year. Considering he scored 4-5 in each of the prior four seasons, we can pretty clearly pinpoint 2024 as the outlier. Additionally, McLaurin saw clear WR1 targets in each of those seasons, because he had basically no legitimate competition for targets at the position — unless you're a big Curtis Samuel truther.

Now, McLaurin finally has a legitimate volume receiver alongside him in Stefon Diggs, who Washington signed late this offseason on a one-year deal. I firmly disagree with those who say Diggs is "washed" — particularly after he logged an 83.3% catch rate, 11.9 yards per reception and 2.4 yards per route run with New England last year. For the first time in his career, I think McLaurin will be more of a 1B, particularly serving as the downfield threat and field-stretcher to Diggs' possession role underneath. With Washington's highly-suspect offensive line, I much prefer the latter role for fantasy purposes, particularly for consistency's sake.

And even if McLaurin has flash games, or is good all year, he opens with a matchup against the Eagles, who allowed just six touchdowns to wideouts last season, tied with the Broncos for fewest in the league. Philly was particularly tough against outside wide receivers in 2025, where McLaurin will likely line up the vast majority of the time.

What to do ❓ For me, McLaurin is outside WR2 range and probably just outside FLEX range as well, in typically sized leagues. He could always hit that one big play to make his day, but if he doesn't, you may be stuck with a four-catch, 50-yard stat line and wish you'd gone with any number of guys on your bench.

Speaking of field-stretchers who need to hit that one big play to matter for fantasy ... I have never been a particularly big fan of Christian Watson. In the 14 career games that Watson has found paydirt, he's averaged 18.1 fantasy points per game and had some extremely high highs. But in the other 34 games of his career, Watson has never seen more than eight targets or more than six catches, has fallen short of double-digit fantasy points 29 times and has averaged 5.4 points per game. In the 30 games he has not caught a touchdown or a reception of 50+ yards, he's averaged 4.6 fantasy points per game.

Across four seasons in total, Watson has one game with double-digit targets and zero games with eight or more catches. Just to contextualize Watson's consistent lack of volume, here's a fun list of guys over that span who do have games with eight or more catches: former teammate Romeo Doubs (three such games), Russell Gage (two), K.J. Osborn (two), Devaughn Vele (two), as well as Gunner Olszewski, Ray-Ray McCloud, Richie James, Isaiah Hodgins, Quez Watkins and Ryan Flournoy (among others).

Could Watson hit that one play against the Vikings? Maybe. There's probably something like a one-in-three chance. But if he doesn't? You're looking at a busted week. And to make matters worse, Minnesota allowed the fewest fantasy points to wideouts last year. Even with Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks gone, and Watson's new contract, I'm not willing to trust it until I see consistently meaningful volume and a more reliable floor.

What to do ❓ Watson's in a very similar spot to McLaurin: outside WR2 range, just outside of FLEX range, very boom-or-bust play. Unless your lineup feels in desperate need of a jolt, I'd rather play a more reliable option like Tony Pollard in my FLEX. Oh, and please start Parker Washington over both of these guys if you have the chance.

Mark Andrews has a long and storied career of fantasy excellence at the tight end position, so it's hard to put him in a column like this ... but here we are. Over the final seven weeks of last season, Andrews averaged 2.3 catches and 20.9 receiving yards per game, with zero touchdowns. He never hit double-digit fantasy points over that stretch, averaging just 3.3 per game. The list of tight ends who outscored him from Week 12 on includes Gunnar Helm, Josh Oliver and A.J. Barner.

Don't get me wrong, the arrival of OC Declan Doyle, departure of Isaiah Likely and prospective rebound campaign from Lamar Jackson could all play in Andrews' favor in 2026. Maybe he has a resurgent season at 31 years old. To me, that seems a little far-fetched, and I'd like to see some believable and sustainable production from the veteran before putting him in my starting lineup again. Specifically, Andrews did not top four catches or 50 receiving yards once after the month of September last season. Unless he returns to form as a go-to target for Jackson, he belongs in the tier of "touchdown-or-bust" tight ends outside the top 12.

What to do ❓ The tight end position is admittedly shallow, so you may not have a wealth of alternative options to Andrews. But he is outside TE1 range for me in Week 1, and you can consider streamers like Isaiah Likely, Juwan Johnson, Dalton Kincaid, Dalton Schultz and Michael Mayer (sans Brock Bowers) over him.

articles.title: Kylian Mbappé reacts to viral memes comparing him to a dictator
articles.summary: The France has been portrayed in military outfits, sitting on a throne, or posing next to Soviet leader Josef Stalin and other controversial leaders
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappé has said he did not entirely appreciate a series of AI-generated social media memes portraying him as a dictator during the World Cup.

The France international was depicted in military uniform, enthroned, or positioned alongside Soviet leader Josef Stalin and other controversial figures.

Speaking to France Football magazine about the images, Mbappé acknowledged the humour, but said he disliked comparisons with individuals linked to historical tragedies.

"There's a part of it that's funny because you can tell that, for some people, it's good-natured," he said.

"There's also a part that's a little less funny because we know the damage that people like that have caused throughout history.

"Being compared to people who murder others, or who have made millions and millions of people miserable. ... I don't think I've done that in my life. So there's a mixture of things."

The France striker, who overtook Lionel Messi for the most career World Cup goals with 22, added: "I know it's done in a light-hearted way and that it doesn't go that far, but sometimes it shows a lack of political and human awareness among people."

Mbappé was reminded that his France teammate Ousmane Dembélé gave him the nickname "Mobut," a reference to the former autocratic leader Mobutu Sese Seko.

"With Ousmane, it's something is different," Mbappé said. "He picked it up from social media. With him, it's just a joke."

Earlier this week, it emerged Manchester United opted against making a move for Mbappe in 2015 after remaining unimpressed by a recommendation from scouts.

According to Ryan Giggs , who joined the coaching staff under Louis van Gaal at Old Trafford after retirement, the club was advised to look at a youngster who was then playing for Monaco .

Speaking to the Rio Ferdinand Presents podcast , Giggs said: They (the scouting team) went to watch him.

"Monaco were playing PSG . So they went to Paris to watch him.

"A few weeks later, I said to this guy (a French contact who recommended Mbappe ), 'How did it go?' and he went, 'Yeah, they weren't too sure about him', so we just left it, and that was it.'"

Mbappe soon made his senior breakthrough at Monaco, helping the club to the Ligue 1 title in 2017 before joining Paris Saint-Germain for the second highest transfer fee of all time and firing France to World Cup glory. He left PSG for Real Madrid in 2024.

articles.title: Alim McNeill looks like himself again: 'I cannot wait to see No. 54'
articles.summary: Whether Alim McNeill, a first-time captain, returns to form is one of the most crucial pivot points for the Detroit Lions in 2026.
articles.body:
ALLEN PARK — For the first time under coach Dan Campbell, the Detroit Lions have more than six captains.

And for the first time in his professional career, defensive tackle Alim McNeill is one of them.

The seven-man crew of 2026 captains — McNeill, quarterback Jared Goff , wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown , offensive tackle Penei Sewell , defensive end Aidan Hutchinson , linebacker Jack Campbell and punter Jack Fox — was determined through a democratic process, with players submitting their nominees on a piece of paper. Those with the most votes received the honor.

"Yes and no," said McNeill on Tuesday, Sept. 8, asked if he was surprised by the recognition from his teammates. "I feel like I worked and put the work in to be a captain, but I wasn't necessarily looking for it when we did it, and they chose me. I'm thankful, grateful."

Whether McNeill can return to form is one of the most crucial pivot points for the Lions in 2026. He was impactful and ascending when the team awarded him a four-year, $97 million extension in October 2024 , but he tore his ACL two months later, sidelining him for the final stretch of Detroit's 15-2 season.

McNeill returned against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 7 last season and performed like his usual, disruptive self, recording five pressures on 37 reps against the pass. That success was short lived. McNeill went on to post only 18 pressures over his next nine appearances, and seven of those came in a loss to the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving. He finished with one sack.

Now about 21 months removed from the injury, the hope is McNeill can bounce back and look like the version of himself that existed before he got hurt in 2024, when he had 45 pressures and seven tackles for loss for a severely depleted defensive unit. His first test will come against the New Orleans on Sunday, Sept. 13, as the Lions open their season at Ford Field.

"I've got to hold back from talking too much about Alim, we'll see Sept. 13," Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard said Thursday, Sept. 10, doing his best to hide his enthusiasm. "I'm so excited for that player. When I say it, it's almost emotional because I know what he wanted to be last year, and he just couldn't. It had nothing to do with, 'Why isn't Mac doing' — no, he just couldn't. A lot of that tape, he couldn't even put his foot in the ground and plant. But he was still out there for his brothers."

McNeill's win rate as a pass rusher in 2025 (10.3%) ranked 38th among 127 qualified interior defenders (minimum 100 snaps), according to Pro Football Focus. He was sixth in 2024 (14.5%) and 29th in 2023 (12.1%).

This offseason, when Campbell compared McNeill's tape from 2025 to his previous work in the NFL, it was clear the defensive tackle was "favoring the leg a little bit, (and) I don't think he even realized it," Campbell said July 31. "I know we're only two days in ... but he does look better," Campbell said in the early days of camp. "He looks like he's back to what he was. He's healthy."

Asked later that week for his thoughts on Campbell's assessment, McNeill agreed, saying, "I was there mentally last year, it (was) just physically, I just wasn't all the way there like I wanted to be. ... You can see it right there, but if you can't get to it, you can't get to it. Now, I've got two legs, and I have no excuse. I feel wonderful out here now. I really feel like I'm back to me."

"I'm just telling you right here," Sheppard said, "September 13th, I cannot wait to see No. 54."

That No. 54 jersey will have a fresh captain's patch embroidered onto it, signaling the belief, admiration and respect members of Detroit's roster have for the player wearing it.

"It means a lot," said McNeill, who added his lone goal this season is to win the Super Bowl. "It means you put in the work, and the guys trust me as one of their leading teammates. I want to take that role on. I feel like I kind of already was in a role like that. But to have the actual patch and everything on the jersey, it's a lot different. It's a huge honor, but it doesn't change anything for me."

▶ Kickoff: 1 p.m. Sunday, Ford Field, Detroit

▶ Records: Season opener for both teams.

images.caption: Alim McNeill looks like himself again: 'I cannot wait to see No. 54'

articles.title: San Diego Wave sign Barbara Bonansea on loan from Juventus
articles.summary: San Diego Wave FC have acquired 35-year-old Juventus forward Barbara Bonansea on a season-long loan until June 2027. “Barbara brings technical quality, intel...
articles.body:
San Diego Wave FC have acquired 35-year-old Juventus forward Barbara Bonansea on a season-long loan until June 2027.

"Barbara brings technical quality, intelligence and a winning mentality to our group," Wave general manager and sporting director Camille Ashton said. "We are excited to welcome her to the club as we continue to push toward the playoffs and finish the year strong."

Bonansea's contract was due to expire next summer. She had been in discussions with Juventus regarding a contract extension that would have kept her at the Italian club until June 2028.

A highly experienced player, Bonansea has been a mainstay for Juventus, amassing 249 appearances and winning 16 trophies, including six Serie A league titles across nine seasons. Juventus secured qualification for the league phase of the Champions League and will begin its domestic campaign later this month.

On the international stage, Bonansea represented Italy at the 2019 World Cup and the 2025 European Championships, opening the scoring against England in the semifinal.

The loan move is similar to that of fellow Italy international Cristiana Girelli , who joined Bay FC in February and has had her loan extended until next summer. Both players are managed by the same agency, A&V Sports.

Pending receipt of her P-1 visa and International Transfer Certificate (ITC), Bonansea will bolster San Diego's front line with seven regular-season games left to play. Last weekend, San Diego named four players — center back Trinity Armstrong, forwards Dudinha and Catarina Macario , and defensive midfielder Kiki Pickett — on its injury list.

Dudinha, who was among the team's most reliable goalscorers, injured her anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) over the summer and will be out for the rest of the season. San Diego signed Macario in March from Chelsea , but the USWNT star has yet to debut for her hometown club as she continues to work through a heel injury.

San Diego has been one of the more consistent teams in the NWSL this year, floating at the top of the table. It sits fifth in the NWSL, level on points (39) with the fourth-ranked Utah Royals, who have an edge with goal differential (10 to six). The Wave are 5 points clear of the Seattle Reign, who occupy the last playoff spot in eighth.

Bonansea will join Wave players like 23-year-old Trinity Byars, who has had a standout season and is in contention for this year's golden boot race. Byars is tied with the Washington Spirit's Trinity Rodman at 10 goals, but they are eight goals behind the league leader, Ashley Sanchez of the North Carolina Courage.

articles.title: Browns Week 1 preview: Behind enemy lines with Jaguars Wire
articles.summary: We get some intel on the Jaguars from their lead writer ahead of Week 1.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns play football on Sunday when they face off against the Jacksonville Jaguars . While the Browns were disappointed with their season in 2025, the Jaguars saw themselves make a big leap and now are entering the new season as Super Bowl contenders.

For the Browns, all eyes will be on quarterback Deshaun Watson , while the Jaguars will look to continue their growth into the top-tier team many believe they can be. Meanwhile, Browns fans are hoping for development across the board from one of the NFL's youngest teams.

To get a better and more unique angle on the game, we asked Jaguars Wire's lead writer Paul Bretl some questions about the new-look team playing in Jacksonville.

Q: How much of an impact would Cole Van Lanen missing the game impact the Jaguars' offensive line in a major way?

A: Any time you're without a starter up front, that's not ideal. That said, the Jaguars may be one of more well-equipped teams to handle that absence, with Walker Little taking over at right tackle if needed. Little has started 39 games during his five seasons in Jacksonville.

Q: In 2025, Trevor Lawrence seemingly discovered his legs with Liam Coen; does that approach carry over to 2026?

A: I would think so. Lawrence's effectiveness with the ball in his hands is a credit to his pocket awareness and ability to extend plays when things break down around him. Going off-schedule then sets up opportunities in the passing game to be exploited.

Who is the ultimate x-factor for the Jaguars in 2026?

A: I define an X-factor as more of an under-the-radar player whose play can have a major impact on the outcome of a game. So to answer your question, I'll go with DE BJ Green. Of course, leading the way at DE are Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker , but at a heavily rotated position, depth is a must, and last season, the Jaguars didn't get enough pass rush production from those behind Hines-Allen and Walker. If Green can carry the momentum he built over the summer into the season, he can have a big impact.

A: The offensive line struggles. This is a good Jaguars team, but the play of the OL unit is one of the question marks entering the season. The Jaguars need to generate more steady running lanes for the backs this season, while giving the quarterback time is the name of the game for every team. A lack of a run game and steady pressure from the defense is rarely a recipe for success.

A: I'll take the Jaguars to win at home. I think that the continuity of being in the same offensive and defensive schemes for a second offseason can provide this team with a jumping-off point after a strong 2025 season. Jaguars 24 - Browns 14

articles.title: US Open Ticket Prices Collapse for First Men’s Semifinal
articles.summary: The get-in for Zverev-Khachanov dipped below $30 Friday morning.
articles.body:
You can watch a US Open semifinal match for about the price of the Honey Deuce.

The get-in price for Session 24 of the US Open—the semifinal match at 2 p.m. ET between Alexander Zverev and Karen Khachanov—dropped as low as $28, down from about $300 at the start of the main draw two weeks ago, according to TicketData . It's a 91% dip compared to just three days ago.

The price dip is likely due to the lack of star power between the two players, even though Zverev is the tournament's No. 1 seed.

TicketData listed its final pre-match average as $40 two hours before the match; pairs of tickets were available on resale sites for $33 shortly after.

The night session match between Americans Frances Tiafoe and Ben Shelton still has a $300 get-in price . It has dipped by 27% over the last three days—ticket prices often drop on the day of the event—but it's still above the tournament average of $296 at the start of the main draw on Aug. 30.

Tickets for the women's final match on Saturday have also dropped in the last day. The get-in price was about $361 before Thursday's semifinals matches to $290 as of Friday morning. The two U.S. hopefuls, Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula, both lost their semifinals match Thursday.

Still, the drop-off doesn't compare to the Zverev–Khachanov match. The finals will feature Aryna Sabalenka, who is looking to become just the third woman ever to win three consecutive US Open titles, against Elena Rybakina, who will take Sabalenka's spot as world No. 1 on Monday, regardless of Saturday's outcome.

The get-in price for the men's final is currently $430, down 22% over the last three days. However, it's unlikely the match will have as drastic of a dip as Friday's men's semifinal given one of Tiafoe or Shelton will be in the match, giving the U.S. a shot at a men's Grand Slam winner for the first time since 2003.

articles.title: Saints restructure another veteran contract to save salary cap space
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints restructured another veteran contract to save salary cap space. Here's what it means for Nathan Shepherd.
articles.body:
We're only days away from the New Orleans Saints kicking off their 2026 regular season, but the team is still working to get their books in order. On Friday, the Saints restructured another veteran contract to open up salary cap space -- this time with defensive lineman Nathan Shepherd . The 32-year old will be a free agent in March.

Before the move, Shepherd had a salary cap hit of $7.12 million, highest of all the Saints' defensive linemen. Much of that came from his $4.77 million base salary, which was reduced to the minimum and paid back as a $3.4 million signing bonus. That means the Saints saved about $2.7 million on this year's books by deferring it to next year.

In the short term, it means New Orleans should be under the 2026 salary cap by about $8 million, give or take a couple hundred thousand dollars. That's going to give them flexibility in-season to send players to injured reserve and sign replacements while churning the practice squad and the bottom of the depth chart. It also means they could get active at the trade deadline in November. But it doesn't mean they're gearing up for a big move right now. They could also roll over unspent cap space into 2027.

But because Shepherd's contract expires after the 2026 season, restructuring him now means there will be more than $7.1 million left behind in dead money next year. That's not a big deal by itself, especially when the salary cap is projected to soar past $300 million. But look at all of the expiring deals (and dead money) the Saints may have to deal with in the spring:

Lump that in with the dead money already counting against them next year (about $1.19 million between Isaac Yiadom , TJ Hall Jr., and Devin Neal , among others) and you're looking at a bill of around $31.32 million. That's chump change compared to the $116.19 million the Saints are paying in dead money this year. But it's still something to keep in mind when we're setting high expectations for another active offseason in free agency.

articles.title: Just days before Eagles opener, Commanders part ways with former first-round pick
articles.summary: Washington Commanders have made a late change to their offensive line just days before their season opener against the Philadelphia Eagles. The team released...
articles.body:
Washington Commanders have made a late change to their offensive line just days before their season opener against the Philadelphia Eagles .

The team released former first-round pick and Pro Bowl offensive tackle D.J. Humphries on Friday, just two days before the Commanders face the Eagles.

ESPN's John Keim confirmed the move on X.

"Washington released (tackle) D.J. Humphries," ESPN's John Keim wrote on X.

The Commanders had signed Humphries to provide depth and starting experience on their offensive line. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported the move on August 30.

Humphries joined Washington after previously earning Pro Bowl honours with the Arizona Cardinals in 2021.

The 6-foot-5, 302-pound offensive tackle tore his ACL while playing for the Cardinals in 2023. He then played for the Kansas City Chiefs in 2024 before spending the 2025 season with the Los Angeles Rams .

Humphries had 101 career starts, mostly with the Cardinals, before his release from Washington.

Humphries now finds himself without a spot on Washington's roster just two days before the team's season opener against Philadelphia.

articles.title: Jessica Pegula falls to Aryna Sabalenka in US Open semifinal
articles.summary: Buffalo native Jessica Pegula's run at the U.S. Open ended Thursday with a 7-5, 6-2 loss to defending champion Aryna Sabalenka.
articles.body:
Buffalo native Jessica Pegula's run at the 2026 U.S. Open came to an end Thursday night when she was defeated by longtime rival Aryna Sabalenka in the women's singles semifinals. Sabalenka, the tournament's No. 1 seed from Belarus, defeated the third-seeded Pegula 7-5, 6-2 at Arthur Ashe Stadium in New York.

Pegula falls to Sabalenka in straight sets

Pegula and Sabalenka traded holds through most of the opening set, with neither player earning many opportunities to break serve.

Serving at 5-6, Pegula was broken for the first time in the match, allowing Sabalenka to claim the opening set 7-5. Sabalenka then pulled away in the second set, breaking Pegula twice en route to a 6-2 victory and a place in the U.S. Open final.

Sabalenka finished with 29 winners and seven aces during the 80-minute match, while Pegula struck 12 winners.

The loss ended another deep U.S. Open run for Pegula, who reached the semifinals in New York for the second consecutive year.

The Buffalo native, and daughter of Buffalo Bills and Buffalo Sabres owners Terry and Kim Pegula, added another Grand Slam semifinal appearance to her résumé in 2026.

Pegula also reached the Australian Open semifinals earlier this year and entered the U.S. Open ranked No. 3 in the world.

Sabalenka advances to fourth straight U.S. Open final

Thursday's result continued Sabalenka's dominance over Pegula at Flushing Meadows.

Sabalenka defeated Pegula in the 2024 U.S. Open final and again in the 2025 semifinals. The 2026 semifinal marked the third consecutive year the two players met during the tournament's final week.

"I don't know who pissed her off today," Pegula told reporters after the match. "Hopefully it wasn't me totally, but might have been. I don't know. She played insane. She played a super-high level. Honestly, I don't really know if there was much I could do today."

Sabalenka advanced to her fourth consecutive U.S. Open final and extended her winning streak at the tournament to 19 matches. She is seeking a third straight U.S. Open championship.

Sabalenka will face Elena Rybakina in the women's singles final on Saturday, Sept. 12. Rybakina advanced by defeating Coco Gauff 3-6, 6-4, 6-4 in the second semifinal Thursday night.

How to watch the U.S. Open women's final

The 2026 U.S. Open runs through Sept. 13 at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Flushing, New York.

articles.title: Big 12 football games to watch in Week 2 of 2026 season
articles.summary: Here is an overview of the Big 12's Week 2 slate, including the game to watch and which team should be on upset alert.
articles.body:
The first week of the season was exciting in the Big 12. Colorado pulled off a stunning comeback against Georgia Tech , while Baylor 's game came down to the final play against Auburn . Oklahoma State also lost in a bit of a shocking upset to Tulsa in their opener. Looking ahead to Week 2, another exciting slate of games awaits.

Best Game of the Week: No. 15 BYU vs Arizona

BYU had a dominant start to the season with their 63-7 win over Utah State, while the Wildcats dismantled Northern Arizona in their season opener. Personally, I have enjoyed watching Arizona quarterback Noah Fifita the past few seasons. The Wildcats also seem competitive, and that showed in the votes they received in the US LBM Coaches Poll . Perhaps if this game were happening a little later in the season, both teams would be ranked. I will also be looking forward to seeing how Arizona deals with BYU's star running back LJ Martin, who had a quiet day in their opener with only seven carries. Martin, the Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year last season, could make this game very entertaining as well.

Potential upset: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. Oregon State

Technically, Arizona beating BYU would be an upset. But the Beavers taking down Texas Tech would be a far more shocking upset.

In a weekend of massive blowouts, the Red Raiders only won their opener against Abilene Christian by 23 points. Now, they face Oregon State, who put up a real fight in their season opener against Houston. This game could easily become a blowout where Texas Tech shows why they are the favorites to win the Big 12 and reach the College Football Playoffs for the second year in a row. However, Oregon State is not a team to overlook despite their terrible 43-181-3 record against AP-ranked teams.

Another game to pay attention to in the Big 12 is when No. 10 Texas A&M faces Arizona State . The Sun Devils tend to play spoiler and just beat a top-10 team, Texas Tech, last season. Even if they aren't playoff-caliber, they're competitive and opponents cannot underestimate them. Arizona State also smoked Morgan State in their season opener with quarterback Cutter Boley throwing for 387 passing yards and six touchdowns. This is another matchup that could give college football its first massive upset of the season.

The Big 12 has one Friday game this week: Kansas takes on No. 23 Missouri. This could be another game that flies under the radar if the Jayhawks are competitive and avoid costly mistakes. After their disappointing opener loss, Oklahoma State will face No. 6 Oregon, which probably will not end well for them.

In other Big 12 news, Kansas State faces another member of the new Pac-12, Washington State, which was also competitive in its season opener. Nonetheless, Kansas State is still heavily favored. West Virginia plays UT Martin and looks for its second win of the season, while Colorado takes on Weber State.

UCF faces a tough battle against Pittsburgh, while No. 22 Houston takes on Southern from the FCS; Cincinnati also has a matchup against a FCS team with West Carolina. Iowa State plays an intrastate game against No. 21 Iowa, while TCU looks for its first win of the year when it takes on Grambling. Baylor is also looking for their first win of the season against Prairie View.

No. 20 Utah will play against Arkansas in the latest game of the Big 12 weekend slate. The Utes are favored to win, and it will be the first time the two have faced each other in football.

articles.title: Minor league baseball: Reading Fightin Phils returning to playoffs
articles.summary: The Reading Fightin Phils have clinched their first postseason berth since 2019 with an 11-10 win over the Erie SeaWolves on Thursday night. Tied 6-6 going i...
articles.body:
The Reading Fightin Phils have clinched their first postseason berth since 2019 with an 11-10 win over the Erie SeaWolves on Thursday night.

Tied 6-6 going into the bottom of the sixth inning, an RBI single to right field from OF Dante Nori and a two-run RBI double from Aidan Miller gave the Fightins a 9-6 lead, one they'd hold on to despite a three-run ninth inning from the SeaWolves.

Reliever Evan Gates earned the win, while Daniel Harper got the save, ending the game on a 4-6-3 double play to break the playoff drought in Baseballtown and earn the Eastern League Northeast second-half championship.

"Definitely it's been fun. We're very happy that right now we're having a good, strong second half, and fans are really enjoying it," manager Al Pedrique said. "The fans of Reading deserve that, and we're hoping that we continue playing well and give them good baseball."

The Fightin Phils, the Philllies Double-A affiliate, will open their first postseason series on Tuesday against the Hartford Yard Goats, Double-A affiliate of the Colorado Rockies , at FirstEnergy Stadium in a three-game series, while their regular season will conclude Sunday against the SeaWolves.

The Yard Goats won the first-half championship with a record of 39-29 but slowed down in the later summer months with a 26-40 record.

Similarly, it's been a tale of two halves for Reading (68-66), as they finished 30-39, 9.5 games behind first place in the Eastern League Division with a -14 run differential in the first half of the season, which spanned from April 2 to June 26.

Since their last playoff bid, the Fightin Phils have struggled in the first halves of seasons, which ultimately bleeds into the rest of the season, but in 2026, that was different.

"I think we learned a lot from our mistakes that we made in the first half," Pedrique said. "I'm very happy that a lot of these guys made some adjustments for what they did in the first half, and I think it's showing the second half as a team we're playing real well."

"Individually, they know what the job is, and that's the one thing they have learned throughout the season that we need to approach it one day at a time and go from there."

That statement holds true, as a switch was flipped in the second half. The Fightins hold a 38-27 record, a +25 run differential and a 23-15 record against .500 or better ballclubs.

It's no secret that Reading has had talent over the course of their playoff drought, with players such as former Eastern League MVP OF Felix Reyes, OF Otto Kemp , OF Johan Rojas and P Mick Abel .

But in 2026, they were able to put it all together, with a lot of exciting young talent that many see contributing in Philadelphia for years to come.

Highlighting this year's group is Phillies No. 1 prospect pitcher Gage Wood, recently No. 2 SS Aidan Miller, No. 5 SS Bryan Rincon, No. 6 2B Aroon Escobar and No. 7 OF Dante Nori.

Wood, MLB's No. 33 overall prospect, was called up from Clearwater in mid-May, and the 2025 first-round selection has played as advertised, racking up 99 strikeouts in 68.2 innings pitched. He'll likely be the Game 1 starter come Tuesday.

Miller, MLB's No. 61 overall prospect, returned from a season-long back injury on Tuesday. Many people, including himself, did not think he'd have a chance to return in 2026, but he has immediately contributed to the ballclub. Miller spent 108 games in Reading last season.

"Just playing to win and having something in line is so fun. That's what we're all here to do. " Miller said prior to his Reading debut on Tuesday. "Eventually, get up to Philadelphia and play for a World Series, so the fact that we're playing baseball for something, it's bigger than all of ourselves. It's going to be really fun."

Another exciting prospect that fans should become familiar with is SS Bryan Rincon.

The 22-year-old has blasted 24 homers, driven in 62 runs, stolen 29 bases and leads the ballclub with a .906 OPS.

The spark of youth, which is consistent for almost all teams in the minor leagues, just has a different fire to it this year for the Fightins.

Pedrique, in his fourth season in Reading, gave credit to the young ballclub for changing their fortunes around.

"Since the season started, we've had good chemistry in the clubhouse. We got a bunch of good guys that play together well. They play hard. They compete, and that's what they've done the whole year … They know the way we're going to approach this is one pitch at a time and one game at a time."

Leading the team in home runs (26) and RBIs (78) is first baseman Alex Binelas, who was recently called up to Lehigh Valley to begin the month of September. But RF Raylin Heredia has put up similar numbers in a breakout season for the 22-year-old.

In his first season in Reading, Heredia, a Dominican Republic native, has 23 homers, 74 RBIs, 22 doubles and a .280 BA.

In the Fightin Phils' past three postseason appearances, they fell in the first round in 2019 and 2016 but did reach the league championship in 2015.

The 2026 ballclub is eager to make some noise come Tuesday against the Hartford Yard Goats, who they've split four series with at a record of 12-12. After the first game in Reading, they'll travel to Connecticut to play the final two games of the series on Thursday and Friday, Sept. 17 and 18.

articles.title: Prep cross-country: Trojans put on memorable performance in Hunerdosse Invite
articles.summary: FAIRFIELD — Brice Boatright was headed back around the course at Waterworks Park on Thursday night. The Fairfield senior was about to head up the hill for th...
articles.body:
FAIRFIELD — Brice Boatright was headed back around the course at Waterworks Park on Thursday night.

The Fairfield senior was about to head up the hill for the final time before making his way out of the woods and down through the open field towards the finish line. Getting up that hill, however, was going to prove to be a challenge.

"I was not going to make it up that hill," Boatright said. "That's when I thought about what Coach (Jerrod) Belzer told us before the meet.

"If you can't do it for yourself, do it for Jack."

The Ron Hunerdosse Invitational proved to be a special night for both Fairfield cross-country teams and the rest of the community. The Trojans, sparked by the inspired runs of athletes like Boatright, finished second among the large-school boys with 92 points while the Fairfield girls placed third with 100 points, just one point behind Southeast Conference rival Fort Madison.

"It's been awhile, especially on the boys side, since we've been this competitive," Belzer said. "It was truly a team effort. Brice is running really well. We've got runners that are brand new to the sport. The girls was also an even bigger pleasant surprise. There were a lot of unknowns with that team. You see kids running in practice, but until they step out there, you just don't know."

Fairfield's impressive performance not came at home, but came on a night dedicated to a former classmate. Jack Polonsky passed away after battling T-cell Lymphoma for three years in July of 2025, less than two months before the start of what would have been his sophomore year at Fairfield High School.

Many of the current Trojan runners that competed on Thursday grew up as a classmate, teammate and friend of Polonsky. Alex Jo Stewart, who led the Fairfield girls by finishing 16th in the Hunerdosse Invite in 22:12.197, talked about the inspiration that Polonsky continues to provide the entire team.

"We're out here wearing gold and trying to show our support to everyone that is still fighting cancer," Steward said. "We want to show the same spirit that Jack showed as we run together throughout the season."

Fairfield returns to the course at Fort Madison next Thursday competing in the Timm Lamb Invitational.

articles.title: Antonelli beats Ferrari to top second practice for F1 Spanish GP
articles.summary: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli was fastest in the second practice for the Formula One Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid on Friday. The Mercedes driver clocked...
articles.body:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli was fastest in the second practice for the Formula One Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid on Friday.

The Mercedes driver clocked the fastest time of 1 minute 33.662 seconds, beating the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc by 0.113 seconds. Lewis Hamilton in the other Ferrari was third.

George Russell, who topped the early session, was only fifth this time, behind the Racing Bulls of Arvid Lindblad, who crashed out of the session.

Max Verstappen of Red Bull was sixth, while title holder Lando Norris didn't participate in the second practice due to car issues.

"We identified an issue on Lando's car, which requires a gearbox change. We are working to try and get Lando back out before the end of the session, although time is very tight," his McLaren team said on X.

After coming from 19th to claim a sensational win on home soil at the Italian GP last weekend, Antonelli tops the drivers' standings 66 points ahead of Mercedes team-mate Russell.

The new circuit in Madrid is making its debut on the F1 calendar and has been described as "crazy," "scary," and the season's "most complicated."

While the first F1 practice ran smoothly, there was a red flag in the second session after Lindblad hit the wall.

He turned into Turn 13 and the rear slid out from him as he slid into the barriers sideways, hitting with both the front and the rear.

In the Formula Two practice, Thai driver Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak hit the barrier at Turn 19 as his car caught on fire, releasing a lot of smoke. He climbed out of the car and was initially unharmed.

The circuit in Madrid it's considered very challenging because of its fast turns, and there are also several sections where drivers can barely see what's ahead of them. Run-off areas are also scarce.

articles.summary: The Detroit Red Wings expect Dylan Larkin to be at training camp, even with his trade request over the summer. Unfortunately, he will not be a captain this...
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings expect Dylan Larkin to be at training camp , even with his trade request over the summer. Unfortunately, he will not be a captain this time around, and there is uncertainty about what his future on the team looks like. In an attempt to clear up things as much as possible, Larkin and the Red Wings have written statements about what direction they're heading in.

"Over the past couple of weeks, Red Wings leadership and I have had several in-depth discussions. I've appreciated those candid conversations, and I will be at training camp with my teammates. When new leadership is in place, we'll talk further about the direction of the team. We will keep those conversations private, and I will keep my focus on the season ahead and on the guys in that room," Larkin said in his statement.

The Red Wings then announced they will begin the season without a captain.

"The Red Wings will begin the 2026-27 season without a captain being named. Any further discussions or decisions regarding this topic will be made once new hockey operations leadership is in place," the team said in a statement.

Larkin had been a captain for the Red Wings since 2021 and has been with the team for his entire career. He's currently 10th in franchise history in goals and points.

There have been a few moving parts for the Red Wings this summer outside of Larkin's trade request. Patrick Kane returned to the Chicago Blackhawks in free agency, and Steve Yzerman was moved from general manager to senior advisor. Yzerman noted that he didn't want to make any guarantees that he'd grant Larkin's trade request, who has a no-trade clause.

Dylan is under contract as a member of the Detroit Red Wings . Any conversations regarding his future with the Club will take place privately when a new hockey operations leader has been named," the Red Wings said.

articles.title: GAA footballer involved in hit-and-run handed suspended sentence
articles.summary: Kavan Keenan knocked down Fiona McGill while she was out walking in Martinstown in 2024.
articles.body:
An Antrim gaelic footballer has been given a nine-month suspended prison sentence after a woman suffered serious injuries in a 'hit-and-run' incident.

Kavan Keenan was driving a van when it struck Fiona McGill, a mother of two, as she walked along the Glenravel Road in Martinstown, Co Antrim in October 2024.

The victim, who was in court for the sentencing hearing, had to be treated at the major trauma unit at the Royal Victoria Hospital in Belfast for her injuries and her rehabilitation is ongoing.

The Judge at Antrim Crown Court described how she has endured "darks days and nights" since she was knocked down beside the driveway to her home.

Keenan drove on and initially denied that he was driving the vehicle at the time of the accident.

But he changed his plea to guilty at the end of last year, a month before he was due to go on trial.

The 27-year-old from Millfield in Ballymena admitted injuring the woman by careless driving and failing to remain at the scene of an accident.

He also admitted driving a van without insurance and failing to report an accident.

The footballer's father had also originally claimed that he was driving the van at the time.

The court heard how the van Keenan was driving left the scene of the collision but police enquiries led them to the Keenan family home in Ballymena.

The damaged van was found parked at the back of the house.

A sentencing hearing at Antrim Crown Court on Friday heard that McGill was walking back to her home just before 21:00 GMT after a social evening at a nearby pub.

She was wearing a red coat and the road was well lit, and the court was told by the prosecution that there was "ample room" for a vehicle to pass the pedestrian safely.

McGill had reached the driveway to her home when she was struck but she did not know what struck her.

She felt "a bang" and was knocked to the ground and couldn't get up. The alarm was raised and as a brother and sister of the victim travelled to the scene, they noticed a damaged van parked along another nearby road.

They stopped and asked the young man at the van for his name and he told them he was Joe Keenan.

McGill's brother challenged him saying "you hit someone and left the scene".

Following this, an older man who had arrived alongside the van, asked the McGill's brother: "Who did he hit?".

Meanwhile, the court heard, Keenan asked the McGill's brother: "What are you staring at me for?".

During a subsequent police interview, Keenan claimed he was approached by a man who was "verbally abusive", a prosecutor told the court.

Keenan also insisted that he didn't realise that the van he was driving had hit a person.

Judge Peter Irvine addressed the court about the physical and psychological impact of the accident on McGill and said "her life has changed dramatically".

He said she has suffered "many dark days and nights" and the impact has also been felt by her two young boys who were aged six and 14 at the time.

Relatives had to take care of the young boys while their mother was receiving treatment and recovering from her ordeal.

The judge said there were a number of aggravating factors in the case against Keenan, including his failure to identify himself as the driver at the time.

He outlined how he had received a "large number" of character references on behalf of Keenan from "various sections of the community" including religious figures, the GAA, other sporting organisations, former teachers, relatives and friends.

He said "a common theme" was Keenan's remorse and he also highlighted the defendant's contribution to his community, good character, no previous convictions, and no issues with alcohol or drugs

The judge sentenced Keenan to nine months imprisonment with three concurrent sentences of three months each.

However, he suspended all the prison terms after considering the "exceptional circumstances" in the case.

articles.title: 49ers news: Does Kyle Shanahan ever want to come back to Australia after travel hubbub?
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers look incredible in their season opener. San Francisco trounced Los Angeles in a 27-7 win that never felt particularly close. Kyle Sh...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers look incredible in their season opener . San Francisco trounced Los Angeles in a 27-7 win that never felt particularly close. Kyle Shanahan was not initially thrilled about opening the regular season with an international game. But getting a huge division win in Week 1 makes everything look a lot better.

Shanahan did not sound surprised to receive questions about the potential impact that travel made on Thursday's big game.

"Win or lose, I know everybody was going to make a big deal about that for either team," Shanahan said, per ESPN's Nick Wagoner. "You never know how much that factors into it. You just try to do the best to prepare for 3½ hours. I liked how we prepared, but more importantly, I liked how we played."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Both teams had wildly different travel plans for this Australia game. The 49ers arrived in Australia nearly a week in advance. Meanwhile, the Rams showed up in Australia just one night before kickoff .

Regardless, the 49ers have to be thrilled with how they performed in Week 1. Especially against a division opponent that is widely viewed as the NFL's best overall team .

Shanahan seemed to enjoy his time "Down Under." But that doesn't mean he wants the 49ers to play another international game in Australia anytime soon.

"It was cool. I would like to come back when I'm not working, though," Shanahan added. "It seemed awesome. Seemed like a cool place. But it's tough when you're working the whole time. … I like 17 home games in San Francisco. Nothing against Australia, just don't like to travel."

Now the 49ers have some extra time to travel back to the US before their next game.

Shanahan won't ever get his dream of 17 consecutive home games. But at least the 49ers will return to Levi's Stadium for their next game.

San Francisco will host Miami in Week 2 at 4:25PM ET on September 20th.

articles.title: Patriots reportedly shot down contender's trade offer for veteran WR
articles.summary: The Patriots were reportedly called by a contending team interested in trading for veteran wide receiver Mack Hollins.
articles.body:
New England Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins has generated trade interest in 2026.

According to 98.5 The Sports Hub's Albert Breer, a contending team informed him that they were more interested in trading for Hollins than Boutte several weeks ago.

"I had a team calling me asking if the Patriots would trade Hollins," Breer said. "This was like four or five weeks ago. And I brought up [Kayshon] Boutte, and they were like, 'No, we would rather have Mack Hollins.' That team was a contender, and you'd respect them if you knew who it was. And the Patriots didn't want to trade him."

Hollins is the Patriots' spark plug on offense. He is already off to a good start to the 2026 NFL season, having led New England in receiving yards in their 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 1 with 51.

The 32-year-old Hollins is the Patriots' tallest receiver at 6-foot-4. In addition to his size, he also gives New England another capable receiver after A.J. Brown went down with a high-ankle sprain in the season opener, which creates a larger need for dependable options in the receiving game.

Hollins brings veteran presence, physicality and special teams work to New England's unit. Refraining from trading Hollins may be a sound option for the Patriots while Brown recovers, in the event that interest in him continues to surface.

articles.title: Lakers Could Shake Things Up Again After Jonathan Kuminga Miss
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers may have another move left before the season begins. Missing out on Jonathan Kuminga did not end the team’s search for another wing, a...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers may have another move left before the season begins. Missing out on Jonathan Kuminga did not end the team's search for another wing, and the next move could affect two players already on the roster.

That leaves the franchise with a decision to make as training camp approaches. The front office can keep its current group, or use part of it to chase the forward help it still wanted from Kuminga.

Lakers Could Put Dalton Knecht And Jarred Vanderbilt On The Table

NBA insider Jake Fischer said the Lakers could still explore deals involving Dalton Knecht and Jarred Vanderbilt . He stressed that Los Angeles has time before making that call, but the team still wants to improve at the wing or forward spot after losing the chance to sign Kuminga.

"I do think that the Lakers are still going to be looking at potentially trading Dalton [Knecht], Jarred Vanderbilt," Fischer said.

That does not mean either player is on the verge of being traded. Fischer's point is that the franchise is still exploring options, with no specific deal reported as imminent.

Fischer also said Los Angeles wants "some type of trade upgrade at the wing/forward spot." That is where the Jonathan Kuminga miss becomes important.

Kuminga signed with the Minnesota Timberwolves after the Lakers were among the teams interested in him. The 23-year-old forward agreed to a two-year deal after spending most of his career with the Golden State Warriors .

Lakers Still Have A Roster Problem To Solve

The franchise already has 16 players under standard contracts, one more than the 15-player regular-season limit. That gives the front office another reason to keep the trade market open as the team prepares for camp.

Knecht and Vanderbilt also offer different reasons for another team to consider them. Knecht brings perimeter shooting and was the 17th pick in the 2024 draft, while Vanderbilt is valued more for his defense and ability to guard multiple positions.

That difference could shape which player becomes easier to move. They do not necessarily need to trade both, but Fischer believes at least the possibility remains.

"I do think the Lakers are incomplete right now moving forward," Fischer said.

That assessment keeps Kuminga relevant even after he chose Minnesota . The Lakers wanted his size and athleticism on the wing, and now they have to find another way to address the same need.

Los Angeles has already reshaped much of its roster around Luka Doncic . The next move could determine whether the Lakers finally fill the gap left after missing Kuminga or decide their current group is good enough.

articles.title: Numbers game: Utah high school quarterbacks are putting up incredible numbers this season
articles.summary: Utah high school quarterbacks like Coy Doman and others are putting up insane numbers nationally so far this season.
articles.body:
The state of Utah has produced some elite quarterbacks over the years whether from high school or college – Jaxson Dart , Steve Young, Ty Detmer, Jim McMahon, Steve Sarkisian – so the place knows the position.

So far this season heading into another weekend of games, high school quarterbacks in Utah are putting up huge numbers, some of the best in the country and there are not only a few of them.

The depth among stat-stuffing quarterbacks in the Beehive State is striking and influencing some of their recruitments as well.

In terms of overall passing yards, Utah high school quarterbacks have an advantage because many of them have played four games when the rest of the country has only played three but, still, their passing yards per game numbers are through the roof.

Through four games, Kingston Wright from Manti , Utah leads the country averaging 404 passing yards per game.

Three of the top five nationally are from Utah as Pine View 's Coy Doman is averaging 382 passing yards per outing and Bear River 's Preston Wilkinson is good for 359.5. Both Doman and Wilkinson heading into this weekend have thrown 17 touchdown passes in four games.

While Wright and Wilkinson have not seen their recruitments take off, Doman's has been especially busy with massive programs showing interest in the 2029 quarterback.

Michigan , Georgia and Oklahoma have been showing a good deal of interest and Doman is now planning to visit all three of those programs this season. BYU , Utah and other programs have already offered the prolific Pine View standout.

"It's going really well," Doman said. "I just need to keep my head down and keep playing well though."

Wright, Doman and Wilkinson are in the top-five nationally in passing yards per game but others are representing Utah as well. Mountain Ridge 's Jaxon Hunt is seventh nationally at 340 passing yards and he's also thrown 17 touchdowns already this season. He's starting to hear more from Hawaii and Nevada.

Mountain Crest 's Brady Muir , Logan 's Easton Favero , Juab 's Price Armstrong and Hillcrest 's K'Von Houston are all in the top 14 nationally.

It's incredible to consider but there are 15 quarterbacks purely from a statistics perspective that are putting up better numbers than the most heavily-recruited QB in the state, Salt Lake City West's Kamden Lopati , who is committed to Michigan .

California is known for elite quarterback play. More are being developed in the Southeast over the last many years. But in terms of production, maybe college coaches who love to throw the ball around should be taking a closer look at those Utah quarterbacks.

"We throw the ball a lot," Doman said. "I've trained with a lot of the quarterbacks here and a lot of their offenses are pass-first offenses."

Atlanta Braves outfielder Lane Thomas was scratched from the team's game against the Tampa Bay Rays on Thursday due to left side tightness. Braves manager Walt Weiss said after the game that Thomas would be placed on the injured list . On Friday, Atlanta officially placed Thomas on the IL and promoted outfielder DaShawn Keirsey Jr . to the big league roster in a corresponding move.

"The #Braves today recalled OF DaShawn Keirsey Jr. to Atlanta and placed OF Lane Thomas on the 10-day injured list, backdated to September 8, with a strained left intercostal muscle," the team announced.

Keirsey, 29, has appeared in a total of 80 big league games, all of which came with the Minnesota Twins from 2024-2025. He's hit just .113 at the MLB level with a .355 OPS. In the minor leagues this season, Keirsey has recorded a .247 batting average and .649 OPS across 109 games played at Triple-A.

articles.title: Padres predicted to sign four-time Gold Glove OF in upcoming free agency
articles.summary: This outfielder would be a fantastic addition to the Padres' lineup and defense.
articles.body:
The San Diego Padres have a new ownership group and might have the green light to spend a bit of money this upcoming offseason to land help in their rotation and the lineup.

When it comes to lineup upgrades, the most obvious issue that needs to be resolved is their outfield. Jackson Merrill and Fernando Tatis Jr. have it on lock in center and right, but left field could use a new, high-quality starter.

That's why Bleacher Report's Joel Reuter is predicting that the Padres will go out and land former Chicago Cubs four-time Gold Glove outfielder Ian Happ as a major upgrade in this upcoming free agency.

Padres predicted to sign Ian Happ in 2026-27 free agency

"With Ramon Laureano sidelined since May with a torn labrum in his hip, the Padres have used nine different starting left fielders this year," Reuter writes. "Will that be reason enough for them to prioritize stability at the position? If so, veteran Ian Happ is a Gold Glove defender with 20-homer pop who could be a great fit."

This potential new-look lineup and outfield with Happ in the fold would be quite the group. Tatis is elite, Merrill has returned to star form after a slight step back, and Happ would be a major defensive upgrade with quality offense as well.

With the Cubs in 2026, Happ has 2.7 bWAR with 110 hits, 23 home runs, and a .219 batting average, a .737 OPS, and a 102 OPS+.

While that OPS+ mark is tied for the lowest of his MLB career, his great defense and hitting are more than good enough for the Padres to invest in him this upcoming offseason.

A.J. Preller needs to upgrade the team's starting rotation this offseason, and will likely need some bullpen reinforcements as well. But the outfield should not be ignored.

If they are willing to spend a bit more to upgrade the outfield, someone like Happ, the 32-year-old veteran who's won four Gold Gloves and is hitting free agency after his three-year, $61 million deal is over, would be a very nice upgrade.

This prediction from Reuter coming true would be a positive outcome for the Padres. Adding Happ to their outfield and their lineup is the exact kind of addition this team could really use.

articles.title: Patriots news: Dre'Mont Jones grabs attention with NSFW shot at Seahawks

articles.body:
Dre'Mont Jones made sure New England Patriots fans had something to talk about. That's even after a brutal opening-night defeat to his former team. Following the Patriots' 13-10 Week 1 loss to the Seattle Seahawks , Jones took to Instagram. He posted an in-game photograph of himself driving Seattle QB Sam Darnold into the turf. The outside linebacker made the message unmistakable by tagging an account handle reading @f***_the_seahawks in the bottom-right corner of the post. The NSFW jab quickly spread across social media.

Jones spent the 2023 and 2024 seasons with Seattle after signing a three-year contract. However, his tenure ultimately ended with friction before he landed in New England . Now a key piece of Mike Vrabel's Patriots defense, Jones appears to have plenty of unfinished business with his former team. His latest post made that abundantly clear.

The Patriots' 0–1 start already carries plenty of frustration. New England's defense dominated for much of the opener. They limited Seattle and knocked Darnold from the game. However, the offense collapsed late as Drake Maye threw three second-half interceptions. The Patriots also lost prized wide receiver AJ Brown to an ankle injury. That added another concern to an otherwise highly anticipated campaign. With Christian Gonzalez recently securing a record-setting four-year extension, expectations remain high in Foxborough. New England now gets an extended mini-bye before hosting the Pittsburgh Steelers . Meanwhile, Jones has added another spark to a rivalry that suddenly feels far from settled.

articles.title: Winners and Losers of Dylan Larkin and Connor Hellebuyck's Trade Requests
articles.summary: They've been the "get me out of here" shots heard 'round the NHL world.
articles.body:
They've been the "get me out of here" shots heard 'round the NHL world.

Since Dylan Larkin and Connor Hellebuyck went public with their desires to leave current situations in Detroit and Winnipeg, respectively, the hockey landscape has been filled to the brim with stories about why they want out, where they might end up, and how things will look once they've been moved.

The B/R hockey types have their ears perked up for just this kind of situation, and have happily weighed in with perceptions of the winners and losers surrounding the dual, high-profile trade requests.

Take a look at what we came up with and drop a thought in the app comments.

While Detroit not made the playoffs in 10 years, not won a series since 2013, and not been truly relevant in the championship chase since losing the Stanley Cup Final in 2009; it's even worse in Winnipeg, where the Jets have never won a title, missed the playoffs entirely last spring, and parlayed a Presidents' Trophy into a second-round loss in 2025, it's fixing to get worse before it gets better.

Larkin was the Red Wings' captain from 2021 to this week and had been with the organization since it selected him 15th overall in the 2014 draft, yielding 276 goals and 643 points in 808 games played since his NHL debut in 2015.

Hellebuyck is equally entrenched in Manitoba's hockey-mad capital city, having been selected 130th overall by the Jets in 2012 and won 345 games across parts of 11 seasons while racking up three Vezina trophies, an MVP, and four All-Star Game appearances.

So, on the best of days, it's going to be demoralizing for those passionate fan bases to see their homegrown stars coming to Canada Life Centre as opponents.

Loser: Dylan Larkin and Connor Hellebuyck

They'll probably both get what they want (in terms of leaving their current cities) and it's not as if either one of them will be scrambling to make rent, so by that measure, they'll be just fine.

But the respective divorces from their teams have been prolonged and messy and completely public, which won't help their reputations going forward.

In fact, ask a casual NHL fan these days what he or she knows about Larkin and Hellebuyck these days, and there's a decent chance the response will mirror "oh, those are the guys who are going to get traded."

And if you think it's been covered to death already, just wait until they show up for training camp in Detroit and Winnipeg (or in Minnesota or Buffalo or wherever).

And now that Larkin has relinquished his status as captain of the Red Wings, the perception scar might be permanent. And that's just on the outside.

Losers: Detroit and Winnipeg Front Offices

Just think how much better it'd be if this thing had gone down differently.

If Larkin and Hellebuyck had not grown disenchanted with their stays in Detroit and Winnipeg, respectively, both the Red Wings and Jets were set up for several more years of service from their (arguably) best players.

Instead, because they've both gone public with trade requests, each and every one of the remaining teams in the league will approach the Red Wings and Jets brass knowing they have them over a bargaining barrel.

Neither team is going to get what they would have otherwise gotten for dealing a player on Larkin's or Hellebuyck's level, which means the competitive oblivions that fueled the trade requests (among other factors) aren't likely to change given the likely returns for the deals when they eventually get done.

Winners: Contenders That Will Get Larkin or Hellebuyck on the Cheap

The flip side of the last slide, which narrated the likely fate of the Detroit and Winnipeg brass when the deals are made, is the glee on the other side.

It doesn't take an NHL savant to realize Larkin is a solid top-six center with 276 career goals and a better-than-50-percent win rate in the faceoff circle, nor does it take an advanced degree to understand Hellebuyck was the league's MVP in 2025 and an Olympic gold medalist last winter.

No matter what contender ponies up the necessary resources to land them, they're going to be bringing in an instant contributor toward a Stanley Cup chase without busting up a roster in return.

Winner: Fans That Want NBA-Style Drama in the NHL

Suddenly, the coolest game on ice is starting to resemble "the association."

NBA fans know that it's a place where the players have the power and can engineer their way out of the cities where they were drafted, so they can play with pals in one place or try to construct a super team somewhere else.

It doesn't always work, but it's always worthy of headlines.

It's beginning to seem a bit like that in the NHL where Larkin and Hellebuyck are following the recent leads of Brady Tkachuk and Quinn Hughes, who went public with desires to leave Ottawa and Vancouver, respectively, and were rewarded with deals that sent them to Florida and Minnesota.

This just in: It's a players market, folks.
